citations.quote:
Work over the field $\mathbb C$ and fix an integer $d\ge 0$
([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]], [[def-commutative-ring]]). Let
$\mathcal F_d$ be the free associative unital $\mathbb C$-algebra on the
$d+(d-1)$ symbols $x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ (for $d=0$ there is only
the unit; for $d=1$ only $x_1$), with its word basis and universal property
([[lem-hh-free-associative-ring-and-relations-descent]]), and let
$I_d\mathrel{\trianglelefteq}\mathcal F_d$ be the two-sided ideal
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]])
generated by the following elements:

- $x_ix_j-x_jx_i$ for all $1\le i,j\le d$;
- $s_i^2-1$, $s_is_{i+1}s_i-s_{i+1}s_is_{i+1}$, and $s_is_j-s_js_i$ for
  $|i-j|>1$, for $1\le i,j\le d-1$;
- $s_ix_j-x_js_i$ for $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$, $s_ix_{i+1}-x_is_i-1$, and
  $x_{i+1}s_i-s_ix_i-1$, for $1\le i\le d-1$ and $1\le j\le d$.

The **degenerate affine Hecke algebra** is the quotient $\mathbb C$-algebra
$$H_d:=\mathcal F_d/I_d$$
with unit element written $1$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]). We keep the symbols
$x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ for their images, and for $w\in S_d$ we write
$w$ for the image in $H_d$ of any word in the $s_i$ representing $w$; this is
independent of the chosen word once the basis theorem below is proved. For
$a\in\mathbb C$, the notation $H_d/(x_1-a)$ means the quotient by the two-sided
ideal generated by $x_1-a$.

The verification below establishes exactly the structure of $H_d$ used
throughout this page: the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad r_1,\dots,r_d\ge0,\ w\in S_d,$$
form a $\mathbb C$-basis, so that
$H_d\cong\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C[S_d]$ as a vector
space with polynomial and group-algebra subalgebras
([[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]], [[def-group-ring]]);
$H_0=\mathbb C$ and $H_1=\mathbb C[x_1]$; for every $a$ there is a unique
algebra isomorphism
$$H_d/(x_1-a)\cong\mathbb C[S_d],\qquad x_j\longmapsto a+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j);$$
and total polynomial degree is an algebra filtration whose associated graded is
the semidirect product $\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$ in which
$s_i$ acts by swapping $x_i$ and $x_{i+1}$. The cross relation is
inhomogeneous, so it does not turn $H_d$ into a graded algebra with
$\deg x_i=1$ and $\deg s_i=0$.

Work over $\mathbb C$. Let $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a partition
of $N$ with transpose $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l\ge0$, so that $l=p_n$ is the number
of columns, and let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$ with matrix units
$e_{i,j}$ in the standard basis
$v_1,\dots,v_N$ ([[def-classical-complex-matrix-lie-algebras]]). Number the
boxes of the diagram of $\lambda$ by $1,\dots,N$ down columns from the left,
and for a box $i$ write $\mathrm{row}(i),\mathrm{col}(i)$ for its row and
column, $L(i)$ for the box immediately to its left (or $\emptyset$ if absent),
and $R(i)$ for the box immediately to its right (or $\emptyset$ if absent).
Define the nilpotent endomorphism
$$e=\sum_{i:\ L(i)\ne\emptyset}e_{L(i),i}\in\mathfrak g,\qquad ev_i=v_{L(i)},$$
and declare $\deg e_{i,j}=\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i)$ for all $i,j$, so
that $\mathfrak g=\bigoplus_{r\in\mathbb Z}\mathfrak g_r$ with
$\mathfrak g_r=\operatorname{span}\{e_{i,j}:\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i)=r\}$.
Put
$$\mathfrak p=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}\mathfrak g_r,\qquad \mathfrak h=\mathfrak g_0,\qquad \mathfrak m=\bigoplus_{r<0}\mathfrak g_r,$$
and for rows $1\le i,j\le n$ define the shift $s_{i,j}=p_j-p_i$ if $i\le j$
and $s_{i,j}=0$ if $i\ge j$, together with the centralizer elements
$$e_{i,j;r}=\sum_{\substack{\mathrm{row}(h)=i,\ \mathrm{row}(k)=j\\ \mathrm{col}(k)-\mathrm{col}(h)=r}}e_{h,k} \qquad(s_{i,j}\le r<p_j).$$
Finally let $\chi\colon\mathfrak m\to\mathbb C$ be $\chi(x)=\operatorname{tr}(xe)$,
where the trace is the trace of the $N\times N$ matrix.

The verification below records the properties of this data that are used
throughout this page. $e\in\mathfrak g_1$ has Jordan type $\lambda$; $\mathfrak p$
is a parabolic subalgebra with Levi factor
$\mathfrak h\cong\mathfrak{gl}_{q_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{q_l}$ and
nilradical $\bigoplus_{r>0}\mathfrak g_r$, while $\mathfrak m$ is the
nilradical of the opposite parabolic; the elements $e_{i,j;r}$ with
$s_{i,j}\le r<p_j$ form a basis of the centralizer
$\mathfrak g^e=\{X\in\mathfrak g:[X,e]=0\}$; the box set
$J=\{(a,b)\in\{1,\dots,N\}^2:\mathrm{col}(a)\le\mathrm{col}(b),\ R(b)=\emptyset\}$
is in bijection with $K=\{(i,j,r):1\le i,j\le n,\ s_{i,j}\le r<p_j\}$ via
$(a,b)\mapsto(\mathrm{row}(a),\mathrm{row}(b),\mathrm{col}(b)-\mathrm{col}(a))$, and
$$\xi_{a,b}:=\sum_{t=0}^{\mathrm{col}(a)-1}e_{L^t(a),L^t(b)}=e_{\mathrm{row}(a),\mathrm{row}(b);\mathrm{col}(b)-\mathrm{col}(a)};$$
and $\chi$ is a Lie algebra character, $\chi([\mathfrak m,\mathfrak m])=0$. This
grading is the type-A pyramid good grading of the source, not the Dynkin
grading attached to an $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triple.

Keep the type-A pyramid data
$(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak h,\mathfrak m,e,\chi)$ of
[[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]], with
$\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$, transpose
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, and $\chi(x)=\operatorname{tr}(xe)$ on $\mathfrak m$.
Let $\eta\colon U(\mathfrak p)\to U(\mathfrak p)$ be the algebra automorphism
with
$$\eta(e_{i,j})=e_{i,j}+\delta_{i,j}\bigl(n-q_{\mathrm{col}(j)}-q_{\mathrm{col}(j)+1}-\cdots-q_l\bigr)$$
for all matrix units $e_{i,j}\in\mathfrak p$. Let $I_\chi$ be the kernel of the
algebra homomorphism $\chi\colon U(\mathfrak m)\to\mathbb C$ extending the Lie
character $\chi$, that is, the two-sided ideal generated by $x-\chi(x)$,
$x\in\mathfrak m$ ([[def-universal-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]),
and let $U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ be the left ideal it generates in
$U(\mathfrak g)$.

The **type-A finite W-algebra** is
$$W(\lambda)=\{u\in U(\mathfrak p):[x,\eta(u)]\in U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi\ \text{for all }x\in\mathfrak m\}.$$
It is a subalgebra of $U(\mathfrak p)$, and
$Q_\chi=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ is a
$(U(\mathfrak g),W(\lambda))$-bimodule with right action
$u\cdot\bar v=\overline{v\,\eta(u)}$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]).

The **Whittaker category** $\mathcal C(\lambda)$ is the category of
$\mathfrak g$-modules on which $x-\chi(x)$ acts locally nilpotently for every
$x\in\mathfrak m$ ([[def-representation-of-a-lie-algebra]]). For
$M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$ the **Whittaker vectors**
$$\mathrm{Wh}(M)=\{v\in M:xv=\chi(x)v\ \text{for all }x\in\mathfrak m\}$$
form a $W(\lambda)$-module with $u\cdot v=\eta(u)v$, and
$\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$.

The verification below establishes the algebra and module structures just
stated. The associated graded of the loop filtration on $U(\mathfrak p)$ makes
$W(\lambda)$ a filtered deformation of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$; that statement is
proved later on this page
([[thm-the-loop-filtration-on-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-has-associated-graded-u-of-g-e]]),
and the filtration used is the loop (good) filtration, not the Kazhdan
filtration.

Let $x_1,\dots,x_r$ be an ordered basis of a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$. Then the monomials

$$x_1^{a_1}x_2^{a_2}\cdots x_r^{a_r} \qquad (a_i\in \mathbb N_0)$$

form a basis of $U(\mathfrak g)$. In particular, multiplication identifies $\operatorname{gr}U(\mathfrak g)$ with the symmetric algebra $S(\mathfrak g)$ on the symbols of the $x_i$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]], inherited from assertion (2) of the good-grading cohomology supplier.

Let $(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak h,\mathfrak m,e,\chi)$, $W(\lambda)$,
$Q_\chi$ and $\mathcal C(\lambda)$ be as in
[[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]]. Then the functor
$$Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}-\colon W(\lambda)\text{-mod}\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$$
is an equivalence of categories, with inverse the Whittaker-vector functor
$\mathrm{Wh}$; in particular $\mathrm{Wh}$ is exact and
$\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$ for $M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$.

For every finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $X$, the exact functor
$?\otimes X\colon\mathcal C(\lambda)\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$ transports to the
exact functor
$$M\circledast X=\mathrm{Wh}\bigl((Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M)\otimes X\bigr)$$
on $W(\lambda)$-mod, and whenever $M$ is a $\mathfrak p$-module viewed as a
$W(\lambda)$-module by restriction, the natural map
$$\mu_{M,X}\colon M\circledast X\to M\otimes X,\qquad (\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes m)\otimes x\mapsto um\otimes x,$$
is an isomorphism of $W(\lambda)$-modules. The associativity isomorphisms
$(M\circledast X)\circledast Y\cong M\circledast(X\otimes Y)$ are compatible,
and for the one-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module $\mathbb C_c$ the resulting
isomorphism $\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to V_c^{\otimes d}$
is independent of the order of the composed associativity isomorphisms.

Let $N\ge1$, let $M$ be a $\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$-module, let
$V=\mathbb C^N$ be the natural module, and on $M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ use the
operators $x_j=\Omega_{0j}+\sum_{k<j}P_{kj}$ and $s_i=P_{i,i+1}$ of
[[def-arakawa-suzuki-casimir-operators-on-tensor-functors]]. Then:

1. The operators $x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ commute with the
   $\mathfrak g$-action and are natural in $M$, and satisfy all the defining
   relations of the degenerate affine Hecke algebra
   [[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]]: the Coxeter relations for the
   $s_i$; $s_ix_j=x_js_i$ for $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$; $s_ix_{i+1}=x_is_i+1$ and
   $x_{i+1}s_i=s_ix_i+1$; and the polynomial commutation $[x_i,x_j]=0$.
2. Consequently they define, via the generator-fixing anti-involution of the
   Hecke algebra, a natural right $H_d$-action on $M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$
   commuting with the left $\mathfrak g$-action.

The commutation of the $x_i$ is an independent check: it does not follow from
the braid relations of the $s_i$ alone.

Let $A$ be a unital algebra with an increasing **multiplicative filtration**

$$0=F_{-1}A\subseteq F_0A\subseteq F_1A\subseteq\cdots,$$

where $1\in F_0A$ and $(F_mA)(F_nA)\subseteq F_{m+n}A$. Its
**associated graded algebra** is

$$\operatorname{gr}_F A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}F_nA/F_{n-1}A,$$

with multiplication on homogeneous classes

$$ (a+F_{m-1}A)(b+F_{n-1}A)=ab+F_{m+n-1}A.$$

This product is well-defined. Indeed, if $a$ changes by
$u\in F_{m-1}A$ and $b$ by $v\in F_{n-1}A$, the product changes by
$ub+av+uv\in F_{m+n-1}A$. Associativity and the unit class descend from $A$.

derivations.claim: Bounded spanning in every variable. For each $r$, put $w_r=s_{r-1}\cdots s_1$ (and $w_1=1$). In the affine algebra the cross relations give $w_rx_1w_r^{-1}=x_r+$ terms of polynomial degree zero. Hence $w_rf(x_1)w_r^{-1}=x_r^l+$ terms of degree at most $l-1$. This element is zero in $A$. Every affine ordered monomial with an exponent at least $l$ can therefore have a factor $x_r^l$ replaced by terms of strictly smaller total polynomial degree; straightening those terms never increases that degree. Induction on total degree, applied to every such replacement, expresses every monomial as a linear combination of $x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w$ with $0\le r_i<l$. The same induction proves that $F_mA$ is spanned by bounded monomials of degree at most $m$.

Restrict this module to $W$ and use F3 with $X=V^{\otimes d}$. Restrict the affine Hecke operators on $(Q_\chi\otimes_W\mathbb C_{\mathbf a})\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ to Whittaker vectors, then transport through F3. This defines an affine Hecke action on $V_{\mathbf a}^{\otimes d}=\mathbb C_{\mathbf a}\otimes V^{\otimes d}$; the $s_i$ are place permutations. The following step computes $x_1$ before asserting any quotient factorization.

The transported first operator. Write $Q_c=Q_\chi\otimes_W\mathbb C_{\mathbf a}$ and define $\pi_c:Q_c\to\mathbb C$ by $\pi_c(\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes1)=u\cdot1$. It is well defined: the right $W$-relations become multiplication by the restricted character, and PBW gives representatives $\eta(u)1_\chi$. For a tensor basis vector $v_{\mathbf j}$ write its unique Whittaker preimage under F3 as $z=\sum_{\mathbf i}z_{\mathbf i}\otimes v_{\mathbf i}$, with $z_{\mathbf i}\in Q_c$. Then $\pi_c(z_{\mathbf i})=\delta_{\mathbf i,\mathbf j}$. If $\mathrm{col}(a)\le\mathrm{col}(b)$, then $E_{ab}\in\mathfrak p$ and $\pi_c(E_{ab}z_{\mathbf i})=\delta_{ab}(a_{\mathrm{col}(a)}+\sum_{h\ge\mathrm{col}(a)}q_h-n)\delta_{\mathbf i,\mathbf j}$, since $\eta^{-1}(E_{ab})=E_{ab}-\delta_{ab}(n-\sum_{h\ge\mathrm{col}(a)}q_h)$. If $\mathrm{col}(a)>\mathrm{col}(b)$, the Whittaker equation for $E_{ab}$ instead gives $E_{ab}z_{\mathbf i}=\chi(E_{ab})z_{\mathbf i}-\sum_{\mathbf k}z_{\mathbf k}$, where $\mathbf k$ runs over tensors obtained from $\mathbf i$ by replacing an occurrence of $a$ by $b$. Apply $\pi_c\otimes1$ to $\Omega_{01}z=\sum_{a,b,\mathbf i}E_{ab}z_{\mathbf i}\otimes E_{ba}^{(1)}v_{\mathbf i}$. The terms with $\mathrm{col}(a)\le\mathrm{col}(b)$ give $(a_{\mathrm{col}(j_1)}+\sum_{h\ge\mathrm{col}(j_1)}q_h-n)v_{\mathbf j}$. The $\chi$ term gives $v_{L_1(\mathbf j)}$, because $\chi(E_{ab})=1$ exactly when $b=L(a)$. In the negative sum, replacing the first occurrence gives $-\sum_{h>\mathrm{col}(j_1)}q_h\,v_{\mathbf j}$; replacing an occurrence in position $k>1$ gives $-v_{\mathbf j\cdot(1\ k)}$ exactly when $\mathrm{col}(j_k)<\mathrm{col}(j_1)$. Consequently the transported right action is
$$v_{\mathbf j}x_1=v_{L_1(\mathbf j)}+(a_{\mathrm{col}(j_1)}+q_{\mathrm{col}(j_1)}-n)v_{\mathbf j}-\sum_{k>1:\ \mathrm{col}(j_k)<\mathrm{col}(j_1)}v_{\mathbf j\cdot(1\ k)}.$$
Here a nonexistent left-shift term is zero. In our rectangle $q_j=n$, so the diagonal coefficient is precisely $a_{\mathrm{col}(j_1)}$.

The cyclotomic relation and the leading symbols. Let $C_k$ be the span of tensors whose first entry has column at most $k$, with $C_0=0$. Step 1.3 gives $C_k(x_1-a_k)\subseteq C_{k-1}$: both the left shift and every exchange strictly lower the first column, while $x_1$ preserves $C_{k-1}$. Thus successively applying $(x_1-a_l),\ldots,(x_1-a_1)$ kills $C_l=V^{\otimes d}$. The factors commute, so $f(x_1)=0$ and the action factors through $A$. Grade $V$ by $\deg v_b=l-\mathrm{col}(b)$ and give its endomorphism algebra the induced filtration. In step 1.3 the left shift has degree one and every other term has total tensor degree zero. Hence $\operatorname{gr}_1x_1=e_1$. The recursion $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$ shows by induction that all $x_j$ are filtered of degree one with leading symbol $e_j$, and that $s_j$ have degree zero with symbols the place permutations.

Independence and the associated graded algebra. The cross relations and the conjugated relations in step 1.1 give a surjection $B=\mathbb C[X_1,\ldots,X_d]/(X_1^l,\ldots,X_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{gr}A$. Its composite with the associated graded tensor representation is $X_j\mapsto e_j$, $w\mapsto$ place permutation. Choose the rightmost box in each of $d$ distinct rows and let $v$ be the tensor of those boxes. For bounded $\mathbf r$ and $w$, the vectors $v e_1^{r_1}\cdots e_d^{r_d}w$ are distinct tensor basis vectors: their row labels identify the permutation, and their columns identify all $r_i$. Therefore this composite is injective. It follows that $B\cong\operatorname{gr}A$. Taking leading symbols of a hypothetical linear relation among bounded monomials, first in its largest total degree and then inductively, proves their independence. Along with step 1.1 this gives the claimed PBW basis, its filtration compatibility, and $\dim A=l^dd!$. The longest strings have length $l$, the number of columns, and there are $n=q_l\ge d$ of them; no column height is used as their length. For $d=0$ the algebra, basis and associated graded are all $\mathbb C$, so the assertions hold directly.

Integral roots and the pyramid dictionary. For integral roots write $m_i=\#\{j:a_j=i\}$; then $f(x_1)=\prod_i(x_1-i)^{m_i}$, the quotient attached to $\Lambda=\sum_i m_i\Lambda_i$. For arbitrary complex roots the same algebraic definition applies, with integer-chain bookkeeping separately in each coset of $\mathbb C/\mathbb Z$. The rectangle above has $c_j=a_j$ and $q_j=n$, hence $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$; the general pyramid dictionary is the displayed diagonal term of step 1.3. No general complex root is identified with an integer-only fundamental-weight index.

Level one and the anti-involution. For $l=1$, $x_1=a_1$ and $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$ give $x_j=a_1+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j)$ by induction; the basis of step 3.1 identifies the quotient with $\mathbb C[S_d]$. The generator-fixing anti-involution fixes $f(x_1)$ and preserves its two-sided ideal, so descends to $A$.

The graded top pairing. Put $D=d(l-1)$ and $T=x_1^{l-1}\cdots x_d^{l-1}$. Let $\tau_0:B\to\mathbb C$ be the coefficient of $X_1^{l-1}\cdots X_d^{l-1}\cdot1$. For graded monomials $X^{\mathbf r}w,X^{\mathbf s}v$, this coefficient is one exactly when $wv=1$ and $\mathbf r+w(\mathbf s)=(l-1,\ldots,l-1)$, and is zero otherwise. The equivalent reversed condition is $vw=1$ and $\mathbf s+w^{-1}(\mathbf r)=(l-1,\ldots,l-1)$; thus $\tau_0$ is symmetric. Each basis element pairs with its unique complementary element, so the pairing is perfect, including between degrees $m$ and $D-m$. This establishes cyclicity only under the stated degree bound so far.

citations.quote:
Work over $\mathbb C$. Let $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a partition
of $N$ with transpose $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l\ge0$, so that $l=p_n$ is the number
of columns, and let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$ with matrix units
$e_{i,j}$ in the standard basis
$v_1,\dots,v_N$ ([[def-classical-complex-matrix-lie-algebras]]). Number the
boxes of the diagram of $\lambda$ by $1,\dots,N$ down columns from the left,
and for a box $i$ write $\mathrm{row}(i),\mathrm{col}(i)$ for its row and
column, $L(i)$ for the box immediately to its left (or $\emptyset$ if absent),
and $R(i)$ for the box immediately to its right (or $\emptyset$ if absent).
Define the nilpotent endomorphism
$$e=\sum_{i:\ L(i)\ne\emptyset}e_{L(i),i}\in\mathfrak g,\qquad ev_i=v_{L(i)},$$
and declare $\deg e_{i,j}=\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i)$ for all $i,j$, so
that $\mathfrak g=\bigoplus_{r\in\mathbb Z}\mathfrak g_r$ with
$\mathfrak g_r=\operatorname{span}\{e_{i,j}:\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i)=r\}$.
Put
$$\mathfrak p=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}\mathfrak g_r,\qquad \mathfrak h=\mathfrak g_0,\qquad \mathfrak m=\bigoplus_{r<0}\mathfrak g_r,$$
and for rows $1\le i,j\le n$ define the shift $s_{i,j}=p_j-p_i$ if $i\le j$
and $s_{i,j}=0$ if $i\ge j$, together with the centralizer elements
$$e_{i,j;r}=\sum_{\substack{\mathrm{row}(h)=i,\ \mathrm{row}(k)=j\\ \mathrm{col}(k)-\mathrm{col}(h)=r}}e_{h,k} \qquad(s_{i,j}\le r<p_j).$$
Finally let $\chi\colon\mathfrak m\to\mathbb C$ be $\chi(x)=\operatorname{tr}(xe)$,
where the trace is the trace of the $N\times N$ matrix.

The verification below records the properties of this data that are used
throughout this page. $e\in\mathfrak g_1$ has Jordan type $\lambda$; $\mathfrak p$
is a parabolic subalgebra with Levi factor
$\mathfrak h\cong\mathfrak{gl}_{q_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{q_l}$ and
nilradical $\bigoplus_{r>0}\mathfrak g_r$, while $\mathfrak m$ is the
nilradical of the opposite parabolic; the elements $e_{i,j;r}$ with
$s_{i,j}\le r<p_j$ form a basis of the centralizer
$\mathfrak g^e=\{X\in\mathfrak g:[X,e]=0\}$; the box set
$J=\{(a,b)\in\{1,\dots,N\}^2:\mathrm{col}(a)\le\mathrm{col}(b),\ R(b)=\emptyset\}$
is in bijection with $K=\{(i,j,r):1\le i,j\le n,\ s_{i,j}\le r<p_j\}$ via
$(a,b)\mapsto(\mathrm{row}(a),\mathrm{row}(b),\mathrm{col}(b)-\mathrm{col}(a))$, and
$$\xi_{a,b}:=\sum_{t=0}^{\mathrm{col}(a)-1}e_{L^t(a),L^t(b)}=e_{\mathrm{row}(a),\mathrm{row}(b);\mathrm{col}(b)-\mathrm{col}(a)};$$
and $\chi$ is a Lie algebra character, $\chi([\mathfrak m,\mathfrak m])=0$. This
grading is the type-A pyramid good grading of the source, not the Dynkin
grading attached to an $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triple.

Keep the type-A pyramid data
$(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak h,\mathfrak m,e,\chi)$ of
[[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]], with
$\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$, transpose
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, and $\chi(x)=\operatorname{tr}(xe)$ on $\mathfrak m$.
Let $\eta\colon U(\mathfrak p)\to U(\mathfrak p)$ be the algebra automorphism
with
$$\eta(e_{i,j})=e_{i,j}+\delta_{i,j}\bigl(n-q_{\mathrm{col}(j)}-q_{\mathrm{col}(j)+1}-\cdots-q_l\bigr)$$
for all matrix units $e_{i,j}\in\mathfrak p$. Let $I_\chi$ be the kernel of the
algebra homomorphism $\chi\colon U(\mathfrak m)\to\mathbb C$ extending the Lie
character $\chi$, that is, the two-sided ideal generated by $x-\chi(x)$,
$x\in\mathfrak m$ ([[def-universal-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]),
and let $U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ be the left ideal it generates in
$U(\mathfrak g)$.

The **type-A finite W-algebra** is
$$W(\lambda)=\{u\in U(\mathfrak p):[x,\eta(u)]\in U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi\ \text{for all }x\in\mathfrak m\}.$$
It is a subalgebra of $U(\mathfrak p)$, and
$Q_\chi=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ is a
$(U(\mathfrak g),W(\lambda))$-bimodule with right action
$u\cdot\bar v=\overline{v\,\eta(u)}$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]).

The **Whittaker category** $\mathcal C(\lambda)$ is the category of
$\mathfrak g$-modules on which $x-\chi(x)$ acts locally nilpotently for every
$x\in\mathfrak m$ ([[def-representation-of-a-lie-algebra]]). For
$M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$ the **Whittaker vectors**
$$\mathrm{Wh}(M)=\{v\in M:xv=\chi(x)v\ \text{for all }x\in\mathfrak m\}$$
form a $W(\lambda)$-module with $u\cdot v=\eta(u)v$, and
$\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$.

The verification below establishes the algebra and module structures just
stated. The associated graded of the loop filtration on $U(\mathfrak p)$ makes
$W(\lambda)$ a filtered deformation of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$; that statement is
proved later on this page
([[thm-the-loop-filtration-on-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-has-associated-graded-u-of-g-e]]),
and the filtration used is the loop (good) filtration, not the Kazhdan
filtration.

Equip $W(\lambda)$ with the loop (good) filtration
$$F_rW(\lambda)=W(\lambda)\cap\bigoplus_{s\le r}U(\mathfrak p)_s$$
induced by the pyramid grading $\mathfrak p=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}\mathfrak g_r$ of
[[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]], and
likewise for the shifted Yangian of
[[def-shifted-yangian-and-pyramid-generators-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]].
Then the associated graded algebra $\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)$ is
canonically isomorphic to the enveloping algebra $U(\mathfrak g^e)$, viewed as
a graded algebra via the restriction of the pyramid grading, and the
isomorphism sends the leading symbol of the generator $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$ to
$(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$, where the $e_{i,j;r}$ are the centralizer basis of the
pyramid. In particular $W(\lambda)$ is a filtered deformation of
$U(\mathfrak g^e)$, the loop filtration is separated, and the ordered
monomials in the generators $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$, $(i,j,r)\in K$, form a basis of
$W(\lambda)$.

This filtration is not the Kazhdan filtration: the Kazhdan filtration has
associated graded the commutative Slodowy-slice algebra $\mathbb C[S]$, while
here $\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)=U(\mathfrak g^e)$ is noncommutative in
general.

Work over $\mathbb C$ and fix $n\ge1$ together with a shift matrix
$\sigma=(s_{i,j})_{1\le i,j\le n}$ of nonnegative integers satisfying
$s_{i,j}+s_{j,k}=s_{i,k}$ whenever $i\le j\le k$ or $i\ge j\ge k$, and
$s_{i,i}=0$. The **shifted Yangian** $Y_n(\sigma)$ is the associative unital
$\mathbb C$-algebra ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) generated by the
shifted Drinfeld generators $D_i^{(r)}$ ($1\le i\le n$, $r\ge1$),
$E_{i,j}^{(r)}$, $F_{j,i}^{(r)}$ ($1\le i<j\le n$, $r>s_{i,j}$) together with
the higher root generators $E_{i,j}^{(r)},F_{j,i}^{(r)}$ for $i<j$ and all
$r>s_{i,j}$, subject to the shifted Drinfeld relations of the source (the
shifted analogues of the $D$-$D$, $D$-$E$, $D$-$F$, $E$-$E$, $F$-$F$ and
$E$-$F$ relations, with the shift matrix $\sigma$ entering through the ranges
and the constants). Two filtrations are fixed on it: the **canonical
filtration**, in which each generator of upper index $r$ has degree $r$, and
the **loop filtration**, in which it has degree $r-1$; their associated
graded algebras are different (the canonical one is commutative polynomial,
the loop one is a current algebra).

For the pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with conjugate
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$ ([[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]])
the relevant shift matrix is $s_{i,j}=p_j-p_i$ for $i\le j$ and $s_{i,j}=0$
for $i\ge j$, and the **type-A finite W-algebra** is the quotient
$$W(\lambda)=Y_n(\sigma)/\bigl(D_1^{(r)},\ r>p_1\bigr)$$
of $Y_n(\sigma)$ by the two-sided ideal generated by the higher modes of
$D_1$ beyond $p_1$.

Write the Gauss decomposition $T(u)=F(u)D(u)E(u)$ of the generating matrix,
with $T(u)=\sum_{r\ge0}T_{i,j}^{(r)}u^{-r}$, $T_{i,j}^{(0)}=\delta_{i,j}$, and
**no** additional factor $u^{s_{i,j}}$: the coefficient of $u^{-r}$ is the
mode $T_{i,j}^{(r)}$. Its modes satisfy $T_{i,j}^{(r)}=0$ for
$0<r\le s_{i,j}$, and in the finite quotient also $T_{i,j}^{(r)}=0$ for
$r>S_{i,j}:=s_{i,j}+p_{\min(i,j)}$, so the finite quotient has the PBW basis
of ordered monomials
$$T_{i,j}^{(r)},\qquad s_{i,j}<r\le S_{i,j}.$$
The auxiliary signed path polynomials used in the source to construct the
Gauss generators are not all identified with these shifted $T$-modes; the root
of $T_{i,j}^{(r)}$ is the weight $\varepsilon_i-\varepsilon_j$, and the
surviving modes have loop leading term $(-1)^{r-1}e_{i,j;r-1}$ in the
centralizer basis of the pyramid.

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]], inherited from assertion (2) of the good-grading cohomology supplier.

Let $(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak h,\mathfrak m,e,\chi)$, $W(\lambda)$,
$Q_\chi$ and $\mathcal C(\lambda)$ be as in
[[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]]. Then the functor
$$Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}-\colon W(\lambda)\text{-mod}\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$$
is an equivalence of categories, with inverse the Whittaker-vector functor
$\mathrm{Wh}$; in particular $\mathrm{Wh}$ is exact and
$\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$ for $M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$.

For every finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $X$, the exact functor
$?\otimes X\colon\mathcal C(\lambda)\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$ transports to the
exact functor
$$M\circledast X=\mathrm{Wh}\bigl((Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M)\otimes X\bigr)$$
on $W(\lambda)$-mod, and whenever $M$ is a $\mathfrak p$-module viewed as a
$W(\lambda)$-module by restriction, the natural map
$$\mu_{M,X}\colon M\circledast X\to M\otimes X,\qquad (\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes m)\otimes x\mapsto um\otimes x,$$
is an isomorphism of $W(\lambda)$-modules. The associativity isomorphisms
$(M\circledast X)\circledast Y\cong M\circledast(X\otimes Y)$ are compatible,
and for the one-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module $\mathbb C_c$ the resulting
isomorphism $\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to V_c^{\otimes d}$
is independent of the order of the composed associativity isomorphisms.

Work over $\mathbb C$ ([[def-classical-complex-matrix-lie-algebras]],
[[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]). Fix $N\ge1$, let
$\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$ with its matrix units $E_{ij}$ and the
trace form $B(X,Y)=\operatorname{tr}(XY)$, which is symmetric, nondegenerate and
invariant ([[prop-trace-forms-are-symmetric-and-invariant]]), and let
$$z:=\sum_{i=1}^NE_{ii}\in\mathfrak g$$
be the central element (the identity matrix). The dual basis of $(E_{ij})$
under $B$ is $(E_{ji})$, so the Casimir element of
[[def-casimir-operator-relative-to-an-invariant-form]] is
$$\Omega=\sum_{i,j=1}^NE_{ij}\otimes E_{ji}\in U(\mathfrak g)\otimes U(\mathfrak g),$$
and its operator on every $\mathfrak g$-module is the image under the
representation, commuting with the $\mathfrak g$-action
([[lem-the-casimir-operator-is-basis-independent-and-intertwining]],
[[lem-the-casimir-element-is-independent-of-dual-bases]]).

Let $M$ be a $\mathfrak g$-module and $V=\mathbb C^N$ the natural module
([[def-representation-of-a-lie-algebra]]). On the tensor product
$M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]],
[[thm-associativity-of-balanced-tensor-products]]) label the factors
$0,1,\dots,d$, with factor $0$ equal to $M$. For $0\le a\ne b\le d$ let
$\Omega_{ab}$ denote the operator obtained by applying $\Omega$ in the two
labelled factors, and for distinct $0\le a,b\le d$ let $P_{ab}$ denote the
operator that interchanges the two labelled factors (the flip of
$V\otimes V$ on two $V$-factors). Define, for $1\le j\le d$ and
$1\le i\le d-1$,
$$x_j:=\Omega_{0j}+\sum_{k<j}P_{kj},\qquad s_i:=P_{i,i+1}.$$
Finally put $\Omega^{\mathrm{sl}}:=\Omega-\tfrac1Nz\otimes z$ and define the
Arakawa-Suzuki normalized operators
$$y_j:=x_j-\tfrac1Nz_M+\tfrac{N-1}{2},$$
where $z_M$ denotes the endomorphism of $M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ given by the
action of $z$ on the factor $M$ (so $z_M$ acts as the representation of the
central element $z$ of $\mathfrak g$).

The verification below records the properties of these operators used on this
page: $\Omega$ acts on $V\otimes V$ as the flip; the operators $x_j$ and
$s_i$ are natural in $M$ and commute with the $\mathfrak g$-action; the
recursion $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$ holds; $\Omega^{\mathrm{sl}}$ is the Casimir
of $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ relative to the restricted trace form; and the operators
$y_j$ are exactly the source operators of [AS, (2.2.2)]. For $d=0$ the family
$(x_j)$ is empty; for the trivial module $M=\mathbb C$ one has $\Omega_{0j}=0$,
so $x_j=\sum_{k<j}P_{kj}$ and $x_1=0$.

Let $N\ge1$, let $M$ be a $\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$-module, let
$V=\mathbb C^N$ be the natural module, and on $M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ use the
operators $x_j=\Omega_{0j}+\sum_{k<j}P_{kj}$ and $s_i=P_{i,i+1}$ of
[[def-arakawa-suzuki-casimir-operators-on-tensor-functors]]. Then:

1. The operators $x_1,\dots,x_d,s_1,\dots,s_{d-1}$ commute with the
   $\mathfrak g$-action and are natural in $M$, and satisfy all the defining
   relations of the degenerate affine Hecke algebra
   [[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]]: the Coxeter relations for the
   $s_i$; $s_ix_j=x_js_i$ for $j\notin\{i,i+1\}$; $s_ix_{i+1}=x_is_i+1$ and
   $x_{i+1}s_i=s_ix_i+1$; and the polynomial commutation $[x_i,x_j]=0$.
2. Consequently they define, via the generator-fixing anti-involution of the
   Hecke algebra, a natural right $H_d$-action on $M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$
   commuting with the left $\mathfrak g$-action.

The commutation of the $x_i$ is an independent check: it does not follow from
the braid relations of the $s_i$ alone.

Let $H_d$ be the degenerate affine Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]] and let
$\mathbf a=(a_1,\dots,a_l)$ be a multiset of complex numbers, $l\ge1$. The
**degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is the quotient
$$H_d(\mathbf a):=H_d\Big/\Bigl(\prod_{j=1}^l(x_1-a_j)\Bigr),$$
the two-sided ideal being the one generated by the displayed polynomial
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]],
[[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the tensor-realization verification below; the quotient definition itself is choice-free.

The verification below records the structure of $H_d(\mathbf a)$ used on this
page. A $\mathbb C$-basis is given by the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad 0\le r_1,\dots,r_d<l,\ w\in S_d,$$
so that $\dim H_d(\mathbf a)=l^dd!$; the polynomial-degree filtration has
associated graded the algebra
$\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$. For
integral roots $a_j\in\mathbb Z$ this is the cyclotomic quotient $H_d(\Lambda)$
attached to the dominant weight $\Lambda=\sum_j m_j\Lambda_j$ of the integer
type-A root system, with $m_j=\#\{i:a_i=j\}$; for general complex roots one
uses a separate integer chain in each coset of $\mathbb C/\mathbb Z$, and the
symbol $\Lambda_a$ denotes a formal fundamental weight on that chain, not an
index of the integer-only lattice. The pyramid roots of the finite-W-algebra
constructions are $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ for the origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ and the
pyramid columns $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$. If $l=1$, then
$x_j=a_1+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j)$ in the quotient. The generator-fixing
anti-involution of $H_d$ descends to $H_d(\mathbf a)$. The top coefficient
functional of the monomial basis is a nondegenerate symmetric trace on
$H_d(\mathbf a)$, and it restricts to a nondegenerate trace on every central
block corner.

Let $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a nonempty pyramid with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l>0$, let $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ be arbitrary complex origins,
and put $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ for $1\le j\le l$. For $d\ge1$ consider the raw
tensor operator $x_1$ on the truncated tensor space $V_c^{\otimes d}$ of
[[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]] (whose underlying
space is $V^{\otimes d}$ and whose $x_1$ is the operator displayed there).
Then the minimal polynomial of $x_1$ on $V_c^{\otimes d}$ is exactly
$$\prod_{j=1}^l(x-a_j),$$
including repeated roots with their multiplicities. Consequently the action of
$H_d$ on $V_c^{\otimes d}$ factors through the cyclotomic quotient
$H_d(\mathbf a)$ of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]. The same
polynomial annihilates the action of the ordinary Casimir operator on
$P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$, where $P_c$ is the ground induced module with its
genuine column filtration.

The statement does not assert that every unrelated standard object $N(A)$, or
every parabolic category-$\mathcal O$ object, carries that same tensor action.
For $d=0$ there is no operator $x_1$. The integral-root weight $\Lambda$ and
the arbitrary-root coset bookkeeping are the separate conventions of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]].

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector
space, let $e\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ be nilpotent with largest
Jordan string length $l\ge1$, let $d\ge0$, and put $E=V^{\otimes d}$. Let
$$B=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$$
act on $E$ by the individual operators $x_i=e$ (in the $i$-th tensor factor)
and the place permutations, and let
$\varphi\colon U(\mathfrak g^e)\to\operatorname{End}(E)$ be the algebra map
induced by the diagonal action of $\mathfrak g^e=\{X:[X,e]=0\}$ and
$\psi\colon B\to\operatorname{End}(E)^{\mathrm{op}}$ the map encoding the
right action. Then
$$\varphi(U(\mathfrak g^e))=\operatorname{End}_B(E),\qquad \operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g^e}(E)^{\mathrm{op}}=\psi(B),$$
for every nilpotent Jordan type and every $d$. If $e$ has at least $d$ Jordan
strings of the maximum length $l$, then $\psi$ is injective. For $d=0$ the
identities are scalar identities and injectivity is automatic.

The full converse uses the proved normality and covariant-extension suppliers
of this page; it is not a stable-only claim and it does not assume the double
commutant identity.

derivations.claim: The column-trace function $\kappa_c$ kills $[\mathfrak p,\mathfrak p]$: the diagonal column block of the commutator of two block-upper-triangular matrices is the commutator of their diagonal blocks, and its trace is zero. Therefore $X\mapsto X+\kappa_c(X)1$ respects Lie brackets and extends to the unital automorphism $\eta_c$ of $U(\mathfrak p)$, with inverse $\eta_{-c}$. It preserves the column grading, since only degree-zero generators receive degree-zero scalars. The coproduct gives $\rho_d\eta_c(X)=\rho_d(X)+\kappa_c(X)\operatorname{id}$, exactly the action on $\mathbb C_c\otimes E$; no factor $d$ multiplies the character. Its restriction to $W$ is the stated filtered left action.

Use the actual isomorphism $\mu_{\mathbb C_c,V^{\otimes d}}$ of F3, composed with coherent transported associativity, to identify $\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}$ with $\mathbb C_c\otimes E$. The left action is the one in step 1.1, because the balanced map intertwines $\Delta\eta(w)$ on Whittaker vectors with $\Delta(w)$ on the target. Indeed $(\eta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta(w)=\Delta\eta(w)$ and the evaluation map obeys $\psi(\eta(u)q)=u\psi(q)$. The ambient universal operators $\Omega_{0j}+\sum_{k<j}P_{kj}$ and $P_{j,j+1}$ preserve the Whittaker subspace and commute with its $W$-action; transporting them through this actual map gives a right Hecke action commuting with $W$. Naturality transports the places to ordinary tensor permutations. This argument makes no claim about commutation with the full target $\mathfrak p$-action.

Each $e_{i,j;r}$ has degree $r$. If $r>0$ it contains no diagonal matrix units; if $r=0$ it contains diagonal matrix units only when $i=j$, and then precisely one in each column $1,\dots,p_i$. Consequently $\kappa_c(e_{i,j;r})=\delta_{ij}\delta_{r0}\sum_{b=1}^{p_i}c_b$. Since $\mathfrak g^e\subset\mathfrak p$, the character of step 1.1 restricts to a Lie character on $\mathfrak g^e$. Thus $\eta_c$ restricts to the graded unital automorphism $\tau_c$ of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$, $X\mapsto X+\kappa_c(X)1$, with inverse $\tau_{-c}$. No assertion that $\eta_c$ preserves $W$ is needed.

To compute the transported $x_1$, write $Q_c=Q_\chi\otimes_W\mathbb C_c$ and $\pi_c(\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes1_c)=u1_c$. The evaluation is balanced by F3. For a tensor basis vector $v_{\mathbf j}$, write its actual Whittaker preimage as $z=\sum_{\mathbf i}z_{\mathbf i}\otimes v_{\mathbf i}$; then $\pi_c(z_{\mathbf i})=\delta_{\mathbf i,\mathbf j}$. For $E_{ab}\in\mathfrak p$, $\pi_c(E_{ab}z_{\mathbf i})=\delta_{ab}(c_{\operatorname{col}(a)}-\rho_{\operatorname{col}(a)})\delta_{\mathbf i,\mathbf j}$. For $E_{ab}\in\mathfrak m$, the actual Whittaker equation instead reads $E_{ab}z_{\mathbf i}=\chi(E_{ab})z_{\mathbf i}-\sum_{t:i_t=a}z_{\mathbf i[a\mapsto b\text{ at }t]}$. These two identities compute every coefficient of $(\pi_c\otimes1)\Omega_{01}z$.

The fixed loop chart F2 identifies the graded inclusion of $W$ in $U(\mathfrak p)$ with the ordinary inclusion of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$. The ordinary tensor representation $\rho_d$ and $\eta_c$ are graded maps. Therefore taking symbols of their restriction gives $\operatorname{gr}\Phi_{d,c}=\varphi_{d,0}\tau_c\zeta$. This is equality of the full graded representation, not merely equality of its image. It proves $\varphi_{d,c}(X)=\sum_tX^{(t)}+\kappa_c(X)\operatorname{id}$ and the complete displayed $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$ symbol dictionary. The term $\sigma_i(c)$ survives in degree zero; for positive degree it is absent. The coefficient index, sign $(-1)^r$, finite $K$-range and physical box labels are unchanged.

In that computation the nonnegative-column terms give $(c_{\operatorname{col}(j_1)}+\sum_{h\ge\operatorname{col}(j_1)}q_h-n)v_{\mathbf j}$. The character terms from negative matrices give $v_{L_1(\mathbf j)}$, since $\chi(E_{ab})=1$ exactly when $b=L(a)$. In the remaining negative sum, replacement in the first tensor position gives $-\sum_{h>\operatorname{col}(j_1)}q_h\,v_{\mathbf j}$, and replacement in position $k>1$ gives $-v_{\mathbf j\cdot(1\ k)}$ exactly when $\operatorname{col}(j_k)<\operatorname{col}(j_1)$. Adding yields $v_{\mathbf j}x_1=v_{L_1(\mathbf j)}+a_{\operatorname{col}(j_1)}v_{\mathbf j}-\sum_{k>1:\operatorname{col}(j_k)<\operatorname{col}(j_1)}v_{\mathbf j\cdot(1\ k)}$, precisely the matrix-unit display in the Definition. A nonexistent left neighbour contributes zero. Recursion with the place permutations gives all higher $x_j$, and their affine relations already hold by transport in step 2.1. Thus the displayed action is the transported action, rather than an unrelated action satisfying a recursion alone.

For $d\ge1$ and $l\ge1$, let $C_k$ be the span of tensors whose first box has column at most $k$. The preceding formula preserves every $C_k$ and gives $C_k(x_1-a_k)\subseteq C_{k-1}$. Successively applying the factors from column $l$ down to column $1$ kills $C_l=E$; they are polynomials in one operator and commute, so $\prod_{b=1}^l(x_1-a_b)=0$. This proves the quotient factorization directly for arbitrary complex origins, including repeated roots. In the total grading $\deg v_a=l-\operatorname{col}(a)$, the left-shift part has degree one; the diagonal part and each two-position exchange have total degree zero. Hence $\operatorname{gr}_1x_1=e^{(1)}$. Since the longest Jordan string has length $l$, $(e^{(1)})^k\ne0$ for $0\le k<l$ on this nonzero tensor space. A monic annihilating polynomial of degree $k<l$ would have that nonzero degree-$k$ symbol. Therefore the displayed degree-$l$ polynomial is the exact minimal polynomial, consistent with F4.

The right action is filtered with $x_j$ of degree one and places of degree zero: this holds for $x_1$ by step 5.1 and for each $x_{j+1}$ by $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$. Taking degree-one symbols gives $e^{(j+1)}=s_je^{(j)}s_j$; the extra $s_j$ has degree zero. By F4 the resulting graded right map is the ordinary map $X_j\mapsto e^{(j)}$, $w\mapsto P_w$ on $B^0$. Together with step 3.2 this identifies the entire graded bimodule with the character-twisted Vust module in the Definition.

Since $\tau_c$ is an automorphism, $\varphi_{d,c}(U(\mathfrak g^e))=\varphi_{d,0}(U(\mathfrak g^e))=A^0$ as unital graded subalgebras of $\operatorname{End}(E)$. Equivalently each shifted generator differs from its untwisted operator by the explicitly known scalar multiple of the identity, and either set generates the other together with the common unit. Consequently their commutants are identical as well. By F5, $A^0$ and the unchanged right image $D^0$ are mutual centralizers. This proves the required Vust comparison without identifying the two fixed-chart modules.

Let $C=\Phi_{d,c}(W)$ and $D$ be the algebra of right Hecke operators, with filtrations induced from $\operatorname{End}(E)$. They commute by step 2.1. The symbol maps in steps 3.2 and 6.1 have images $A^0,D^0$, respectively, which are contained in $\operatorname{gr}C,\operatorname{gr}D$. For any commuting filtered operator algebras, taking the largest homogeneous terms of a commutator gives the inclusions $\operatorname{gr}C\subseteq\operatorname{gr}Z(D)\subseteq Z(\operatorname{gr}D)$, where $Z$ denotes the commutant in the relevant endomorphism algebra. Therefore $A^0\subseteq\operatorname{gr}C\subseteq\operatorname{gr}Z(D)\subseteq Z(\operatorname{gr}D)\subseteq Z(D^0)=A^0$. The same argument with $C,D$ interchanged gives $D^0\subseteq\operatorname{gr}D\subseteq\operatorname{gr}Z(C)\subseteq Z(\operatorname{gr}C)\subseteq Z(A^0)=D^0$. Every inclusion is equality. This also proves strict equality of the graded image algebras, rather than presuming that an arbitrary filtered representation is strict.

Since $C\subseteq Z(D)$ and their induced associated graded spaces agree by step 8.1, a member of $Z(D)$ can have its leading homogeneous term matched by a member of $C$ of the same filtration degree. Subtraction lowers the integer degree. The finite grading of $E$ bounds the endomorphism filtration below, so iteration terminates and gives $Z(D)=C$. Similarly $Z(C)=D$. Restoring the right-action opposite convention gives $\Phi_{d,c}(W)=\operatorname{End}_{H_d(\Lambda)}(E_c)$ and $\operatorname{End}_W(E_c)^{\mathrm{op}}=\Psi_d(H_d(\Lambda))$. All arguments hold for arbitrary $c$ and every $d$; no stable injectivity or admissible-origin Morita assertion was used.

For $d=0$, $E_c=\mathbb C_c$, $\varphi_{0,c}(X)=\kappa_c(X)$ and $\mu_0$ is the identity; the right algebra is $\mathbb C$. Both unital operator images and commutants are scalar, even when the fixed-chart character is nonzero. For an empty pyramid the positive tensor powers are zero and both operator image algebras and both commutants in $\operatorname{End}(0)$ are zero; degree zero is scalar. Thus the exceptional cases stated in the Definition are covered without evaluating a nonexistent $x_1$ or invoking a positive-string Vust hypothesis.

In the one-box case $p=(1)$, $q_1=n=1$, $c_1=1$, $d=1$, the fixed-chart loop generator is $T_{11}^{(1)}=E_{11}$, and step 3.2 gives its operator $1+1=2$; the untwisted Vust operator is $1$. Both unital images remain $\mathbb C$, exactly as step 7.1 proves. Separately, for $\mathfrak{gl}_2$, $p=(2)$, $c=(0,0)$ and $d=1$, the displayed $x_1$ is $E_{12}$ and $H=E_{11}-E_{22}\in\mathfrak p$ obeys $[H,x_1]=2E_{12}\ne0$. This witnesses why the correct commutation claim is the transported $W$-commutation established in steps 2.1, 3.1 and 4.1. The full filtered bimodule, coherent $\mu_d$, exact graded character chart and all-origin mutual centralizers have now all been proved.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and that $I$ is bounded
below, so $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are finite; the upper end of
$I$ may remain unbounded. Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n(\mathbb C)$ and let
the standard parabolic $\mathfrak p$ have Levi
$\mathfrak{gl}_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{n_l}$
([[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]).
For a tableau $A$ with column reading $a_1,\dots,a_n$ (read column by column,
bottom to top, [[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]) put
$$\lambda_A=\sum_{j=1}^{n}(a_j+j-1)\,\varepsilon_j .$$
Strict columns make $\lambda_A$ Levi-dominant, so that the simple highest weight
module $L(A)$ of [[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]]
and the induced generalized standard
$M(A)=M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda_A)$ of
[[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]] belong to the genuine
parabolic category $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ of
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]].

Use the published **half-sum convention**
$\rho_j=(n+1-2j)/2$; then
$$\lambda_{A,j}+\rho_j=a_j+\frac{n-1}{2},$$
so the $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ Harish-Chandra shifted-coordinate multiset of the
block is the tableau-entry multiset plus the common scalar $(n-1)/2$, and this
multiset together with the displayed scalar $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ centre labels the
central character ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]). The Fock
weight $\sum_j\delta_{a_j}=\Lambda-\alpha$ of the Fock item belongs to the
different $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ weight lattice and indexes that entry multiset;
it is **not** a literal $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ highest weight.

For an entry multiset $\alpha$ the corresponding **finite parabolic central
block** $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ has labels
$\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$, generalized standards $M(A)$, simples $L(A)$,
projective covers $P(A)$ and costandards $\nabla(A)$, with the BGG reciprocity,
restricted duality and highest-weight structure inherited from
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]; by
[[lem-type-a-tableau-central-summands-are-single-linkage-blocks]] it is a single
linkage block. Its simple and standard classes form bases of its Grothendieck
group, and its numerical multiplicities include repeated-entry singular central
characters. The direct sum over the admitted entry multisets is
$\mathcal O^\Lambda$. **Opposite blocks** use the reversed Levi order and the
reverse-column reading, with the correspondingly reversed label order
([[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
published category-$\mathcal O$ theory. Let
$\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ be the standard
parabolic of
[[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]], with
reductive parabolic Levi $\mathfrak l_J$, nilradical $\mathfrak u_J$ and Weyl
group $W_J$; the ambient category is $\mathcal O$ of [[def-bgg-category-o]]
with standard objects the Verma modules [[def-verma-module]].

**(1) Dominance for the Levi.** A weight $\lambda$ is **$\mathfrak p$-dominant**
if $\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ for all
$\alpha\in\Phi_J^+$ (this is dominance for the Levi root system; in particular
$\lambda$ is integral for $\Phi_J$; see
[[def-integral-dominant-and-strictly-dominant-weights]] for the ambient
notion).

**(2) Generalized Verma modules.** For a $\mathfrak p$-dominant $\lambda$ let
$E(\lambda)$ be the finite-dimensional simple $\mathfrak p$-module obtained
from the finite-dimensional simple $\mathfrak l_J$-module of highest weight
$\lambda$
([[thm-finite-dimensional-simple-modules-are-classified-by-dominant-highest-weights]])
by letting $\mathfrak u_J$ act by zero. Define the **generalized Verma module**

$$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak p)}E(\lambda).$$

**(3) The parabolic category.** The **parabolic category** $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
is the full subcategory of $\mathcal O$ whose objects are the finitely
generated $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-modules on which
$U(\mathfrak p)$ acts locally finitely, that is, on which every vector lies
in a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-submodule; equivalently, every vector
lies in a finite-dimensional
$\mathfrak l_J$-submodule and is annihilated by a power of $\mathfrak u_J$
(local finiteness for the nilpotent $\mathfrak u_J$).

The following structural facts are part of the definition; the arguments are
given in the Remarks.

**(4) Generalized Vermas lie in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.** For each
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$, $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is an
object of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ with highest weight $\lambda$, and the
natural surjection $M(\lambda)\twoheadrightarrow M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$
exhibits $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ as the largest quotient of the Verma
module $M(\lambda)$ that lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.

**(5) Simples.** The simple objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ are exactly
the simple highest-weight modules $L(\lambda)$ with $\lambda$
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral
([[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]]).

**(6) Serre property.** $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is closed under subobjects,
quotients and extensions in $\mathcal O$; in particular it is an abelian
subcategory of $\mathcal O$ stable under finite direct sums.

**(7) Costandard objects.** For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ put
$\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=D M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, the restricted
dual of [[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]].
These are the **costandard objects** of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$; each is
naturally a submodule of the ordinary dual Verma $D M(\lambda)$. They need not
be quotients of ordinary dual Vermas.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$\mathfrak p=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ and $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
be as in [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]. Then:

**(1) (Simples.)** Within an integral block, $L(\lambda)\in\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
if and only if $\lambda$ is $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral; every simple
object of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is of this form.

**(2) (Standards.)** For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the
generalized Verma $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$,
has finite length, has $L(\lambda)$ as its unique simple quotient (head), and
$[M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):L(\mu)]\neq0$ forces $\mu\le\lambda$ in the
dominance order; $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is the largest quotient of
$M(\lambda)$ lying in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.

**(3) (Enough projectives.)** The inclusion
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\mathcal O$ is exact and has a left adjoint
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ (the largest $\mathfrak p$-locally-finite quotient);
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ is right exact and sends projective objects of $\mathcal O$
to projective objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. Consequently, for every
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the object
$P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=L_{\mathfrak p}(P^{(\mathcal O)}(\lambda))$ is a
projective cover of $L(\lambda)$ in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, and
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ has enough projectives and injectives.

**(4) (Generalized-standard flags, BGG reciprocity and duality.)** Every
projective in a fixed integral block has a finite generalized Verma flag. Its
projective cover surjects to its labelled generalized standard with a kernel
filtered by higher-labelled generalized standards. The simple and
generalized-standard classes form bases of the finite block Grothendieck
group, and characters are injective on this group. For $\mathfrak p$-dominant
integral $\lambda,\mu$,
$$(P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=[M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
the multiplicities being finite; moreover restricted duality restricts to an
exact contravariant involution of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ exchanging
$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ and $\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda),\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=0$
for all $\lambda,\mu$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Every simple object
$L(\mu)$ of $\mathcal O$ admits a projective cover
$P(\mu)\twoheadrightarrow L(\mu)$
([[def-essential-epimorphism-and-projective-cover]]), which may be chosen
inside the linkage class of $\mu$; the cover is unique up to isomorphism and
indecomposable. Consequently $\mathcal O$ has enough projectives: every object
of $\mathcal O$ is a quotient of a finite direct sum of such projective
covers, because objects of $\mathcal O$ have finite length and each composition
factor is a quotient of its projective cover.

$\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$, transpose
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, and $\chi(x)=\operatorname{tr}(xe)$ on $\mathfrak m$.

with
$$\eta(e_{i,j})=e_{i,j}+\delta_{i,j}\bigl(n-q_{\mathrm{col}(j)}-q_{\mathrm{col}(j)+1}-\cdots-q_l\bigr)$$
for all matrix units $e_{i,j}\in\mathfrak p$. Let $I_\chi$ be the kernel of the
algebra homomorphism $\chi\colon U(\mathfrak m)\to\mathbb C$ extending the Lie
character $\chi$, that is, the two-sided ideal generated by $x-\chi(x)$,
$x\in\mathfrak m$ ([[def-universal-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]),
and let $U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ be the left ideal it generates in
$U(\mathfrak g)$.

The **type-A finite W-algebra** is
$$W(\lambda)=\{u\in U(\mathfrak p):[x,\eta(u)]\in U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi\ \text{for all }x\in\mathfrak m\}.$$
It is a subalgebra of $U(\mathfrak p)$, and
$Q_\chi=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ is a
$(U(\mathfrak g),W(\lambda))$-bimodule with right action
$u\cdot\bar v=\overline{v\,\eta(u)}$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]).

The **Whittaker category** $\mathcal C(\lambda)$ is the category of
$\mathfrak g$-modules on which $x-\chi(x)$ acts locally nilpotently for every
$x\in\mathfrak m$ ([[def-representation-of-a-lie-algebra]]). For
$M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$ the **Whittaker vectors**
$$\mathrm{Wh}(M)=\{v\in M:xv=\chi(x)v\ \text{for all }x\in\mathfrak m\}$$
form a $W(\lambda)$-module with $u\cdot v=\eta(u)v$, and
$\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$.

The verification below establishes the algebra and module structures just
stated. The associated graded of the loop filtration on $U(\mathfrak p)$ makes
$W(\lambda)$ a filtered deformation of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$; that statement is
proved later on this page
([[thm-the-loop-filtration-on-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-has-associated-graded-u-of-g-e]]),
and the filtration used is the loop (good) filtration, not the Kazhdan
filtration.

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]], inherited from assertion (2) of the good-grading cohomology supplier.

Let $(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak h,\mathfrak m,e,\chi)$, $W(\lambda)$,

[[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]]. Then the functor
$$Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}-\colon W(\lambda)\text{-mod}\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$$
is an equivalence of categories, with inverse the Whittaker-vector functor
$\mathrm{Wh}$; in particular $\mathrm{Wh}$ is exact and
$\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$ for $M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$.

For every finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $X$, the exact functor
$?\otimes X\colon\mathcal C(\lambda)\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$ transports to the

$$M\circledast X=\mathrm{Wh}\bigl((Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M)\otimes X\bigr)$$

$$\mu_{M,X}\colon M\circledast X\to M\otimes X,\qquad (\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes m)\otimes x\mapsto um\otimes x,$$

mode-symbol dictionary is

polynomial/permutation action. It need not be the untwisted Vust module in
the fixed chart. Nevertheless its unital left image algebra and its
commutant are exactly the untwisted Vust image algebra and commutant, as
proved below.

The displayed right operators commute with $W(\lambda)$; full

admissibility or stable-range restriction enters this centralizer assertion.
