Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_N(\mathbb C)$,
with upper-triangular Borel, and represent $a=\lambda+\rho$ by coordinates
of sum zero. For every $i<j$ with $a_i-a_j\in\mathbb Z$, require
$a_i-a_j\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$. Thus $a$ is regular and strictly decreasing
inside each coordinate coset modulo $\mathbb Z$; there is no ordering of
complex numbers from different cosets. Write $P$ for the weight lattice,
$U_\chi=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\lambda$, and
$\mathcal O_{\lambda+P}$ for objects of genuine $\mathcal O$ whose weights
belong to $\lambda+P$.

Let $\mathcal H_\chi$ consist of finitely generated $U$-bimodules $B$ with
$B\ker\chi_\lambda=0$ and locally finite adjoint $\mathfrak g$-action.
For finite-dimensional $E$ let $\Phi_E=E\otimes U_\chi$, with diagonal
left action and ordinary right action. Then
$$T_\lambda(B)=B\otimes_U\Delta(\lambda)$$
is an exact equivalence $\mathcal H_\chi\simeq\mathcal O_{\lambda+P}$.
Every object on either side has a finite presentation by the respective
projective generators $\Phi_E$ and $E\otimes\Delta(\lambda)$. The induced
map is the natural, composition-preserving identification
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal H_\chi}(\Phi_E,\Phi_F)\ \cong\ (E^*\otimes F\otimes U_\chi)^{\mathfrak g}\ \cong\ \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E\otimes\Delta(\lambda),F\otimes\Delta(\lambda)).$$
The comparison commutes naturally with finite-dimensional tensoring.

For $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ the corresponding statement uses
$\mathcal O_{\lambda+\mathbb Z^N}$ and finite-dimensional modules with
integral coordinate weights; $\mathcal H_\chi$ additionally requires its
adjoint Cartan weights to be integral and its adjoint scalar centre to act
semisimply. No assertion here supplies standard-label transport, a
parabolic restriction, or this equivalence for a nonprojective source
Verma or a singular source weight.

Assume AC. Work in genuine type-$A$ parabolic category $\mathcal O$ for
$\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$ with its fixed Borel. Its column Levi has ordered
blocks of heights $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$. All entries in column $j$ lie in
$c_j+\mathbb Z$, where the original admissibility condition is
$c_j-c_k\in\mathbb Z\Rightarrow c_j=c_k$. Use the source highest-weight
convention $\eta_i=a_i+i-1$ and half-sum
$\rho_i=(N+1-2i)/2$, with the column reading prescribed by the source Borel.
For each occurring entry coset $\kappa$ retain its columns in their original
order. Fix an order on the finite set of cosets; no order on $\mathbb C$ is used.

Subject to the local HC tensor-projective comparison stated in [F1], stable
sorting of the coordinates by $\kappa$ gives an exact, complex-linear
equivalence of the genuine parabolic categories, carrying each ordinary
Verma label by the dot permutation and carrying the corresponding generalized
standard, simple head and projective cover. On each linkage block, the sorted
category is equivalent to the product of the corresponding parabolic blocks
for $\mathfrak{gl}_{N_\kappa}$, where
$N_\kappa=\sum_{j\in\kappa}q_j$. Product means the abelian category generated
by finite presentations of outer tensor products, equivalently modules over
the tensor product of the finite block endomorphism algebras.

For the original pyramid with $n$ rows put $n_\kappa=\max_{j\in\kappa}q_j$.
The component integral entry dictionary is exactly
$$a_i^{\mathrm{int}}=a_i-c_\kappa+n-n_\kappa,\qquad m_j=q_j-n_\kappa,\qquad \inf I_\kappa=1-n_\kappa.$$
Thus $m_j+1-\inf I_\kappa=q_j$, with the original nonincreasing retained
heights and charges. For the admitted-ground subcategories, where each original entry has a
nonnegative integral difference from its own ground entry, this dictionary
lands in the bounded-below admitted integral component models of [F4]. For
other genuine parabolic blocks it records the integral weight/coset
dictionary and the trace shift, without asserting membership in that fixed
admitted cut. If the component follows $B_\kappa$ sorted coordinates, its
Levi highest weight and the integral highest weight differ by the scalar
trace-character shift
$$\delta_\kappa=B_\kappa+c_\kappa-n+n_\kappa.$$
This shift is a Lie algebra character and requires no integrality of
$c_\kappa$. Singular repeated-entry linkage blocks are included. The original
complex origins, component entry multisets and their scalar centres remain
recorded; different complex cosets are not merged into one integral block.

Sorting commutes coherently with finite tensoring and its invariant Casimir
and permutation maps. The separated product decomposition is blockwise and
does not assert that unrestricted tensoring is componentwise. The proof gives
its actual filtration and block-projection comparison. Choices of sorting
word with the same stable permutation yield the natural comparison fixed on
the chosen reference highest vector and its tensor-projective presentations.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space of dimension $d\ge0$,
let $n\ge0$, and let $E:=V^{\otimes n}$ carry the commuting left place action
of $S_n$ and diagonal action of $\operatorname{GL}(V)$
([[def-commuting-symmetric-and-linear-actions-on-tensor-power]]). Let
$B:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{g^{\otimes n}:g\in\operatorname{GL}(V)\}$,
and for $\lambda\vdash n$ put
$$M_\lambda:=\operatorname{Hom}_{S_n}\bigl(S^\lambda,E\bigr),$$
on which $\operatorname{GL}(V)$ acts by postcomposition
$(g\cdot\psi)(s):=g^{\otimes n}\psi(s)$ and $B$ acts by
$b\cdot\psi:=b\circ\psi$. Then:

1. **(Decomposition.)** There is an isomorphism of
   $(S_n\times\operatorname{GL}(V))$-modules
   $$E\cong\bigoplus_{\lambda\vdash n,\ \ell(\lambda)\le d}S^\lambda\otimes M_\lambda,$$
   where $S_n$ acts on the first factor and trivially on $M_\lambda$ and
   $\operatorname{GL}(V)$ acts on $M_\lambda$ by postcomposition and trivially
   on $S^\lambda$. The sum runs over exactly the partitions $\lambda\vdash n$
   with at most $d$ rows.
2. **(Nonzero irreducible factors.)** For every $\lambda\vdash n$ with
   $\ell(\lambda)\le d$ the space $M_\lambda$ is nonzero and irreducible as a
   module over $B$ by postcomposition, hence also irreducible as a
   $\operatorname{GL}(V)$-module and as a $\mathfrak{gl}(V)$-module under
   $x\mapsto\Delta(x)$
   ([[def-irreducible-completely-reducible-and-faithful-lie-algebra-representation]]);
   for $\ell(\lambda)>d$ one has $M_\lambda=0$.
3. **(Pairwise inequivalence of the nonzero factors.)** If $\lambda\ne\mu$
   are partitions of $n$ with $\ell(\lambda)\le d$ and $\ell(\mu)\le d$, then
   $M_\lambda$ and $M_\mu$ are non-isomorphic as $B$-modules, as
   $\operatorname{GL}(V)$-modules and as $\mathfrak{gl}(V)$-modules. Thus the
   nonzero factors in the decomposition of claim 1 are pairwise inequivalent,
   and a nonzero $M_\lambda$ is not isomorphic to a zero $M_\mu$ with
   $\ell(\mu)>d$ because their dimensions differ; no assertion is made about
   two zero factors.
4. **(Highest weight $\lambda$.)** For every $\lambda\vdash n$ with
   $\ell(\lambda)\le d$, writing $\lambda_i:=0$ for $i>\ell(\lambda)$, the
   module $M_\lambda$ has highest weight $\lambda$ with respect to the Borel
   of upper triangular matrices: it contains a nonzero vector $\varphi$ with
   $\Delta(E_{ii})\circ\varphi=\lambda_i\varphi$ for all $i$ and
   $\Delta(E_{ij})\circ\varphi=0$ for all $i<j$, and every nonzero
   $\psi\in M_\lambda$ killed by all raising operators $\Delta(E_{ij})$,
   $i<j$, and satisfying $\Delta(E_{ii})\circ\psi=\mu_i\psi$ for scalars
   $\mu_1,\dots,\mu_d$ satisfies $\mu=\lambda$ and lies in
   $\mathbb C\varphi$.
5. **(Homogeneous polynomial module of degree $n$.)** Fix a basis
   $e_1,\dots,e_d$ of $V$ and write $ge_j=\sum_ig_{ij}e_i$ for the matrix
   entries of $g\in\operatorname{GL}(V)$. For every $\lambda\vdash n$ with
   $\ell(\lambda)\le d$ and every basis of $M_\lambda$, each matrix
   coefficient $g\mapsto\langle\psi^*,g\cdot\psi\rangle$ of the action on
   $M_\lambda$ is a homogeneous polynomial of degree $n$ in the entries
   $g_{ij}$.

All statements are over $\mathbb C$.

For $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ over $\mathbb C$, a nonzero $S_n$-map
$\phi:S^\lambda\to M^\mu$ implies $\lambda\unrhd\mu$. At $\mu=\lambda$,
every $S_n$-map $S^\lambda\to M^\lambda$ is a scalar multiple of the
inclusion; equivalently,
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C[S_n]}(S^\lambda,M^\lambda)\cong\mathbb C.$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For every dominant
integral weight $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$, the character of the finite-dimensional
simple module $L(\lambda)$ is
$$\operatorname{ch}L(\lambda)=A(\lambda+\rho)\cdot A(\rho)^{-1}=\Bigl(\sum_{w\in W}(-1)^{\ell(w)}e^{w(\lambda+\rho)}\Bigr)\Big/\Bigl(e^{\rho}\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}(1-e^{-\alpha})\Bigr),$$
the quotient being taken in the completed character ring $\mathcal R$ of
[[def-completed-formal-character-ring-for-downward-cones]], where
$A(\rho)$ is invertible with inverse
$e^{-\rho}\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}(1-e^{-\alpha})^{-1}$
([[thm-weyl-denominator-identity]],
[[lem-geometric-series-invertibility-in-the-completed-character-ring]]). No
quotient of ordinary functions is intended before this formal cancellation is
justified.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For all weights
$\lambda$ and $\mu$,
$$(P(\lambda):\Delta(\mu))=[\Delta(\mu):L(\lambda)]=[M(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
where $P(\lambda)$ is the projective cover of $L(\lambda)$, the left-hand
multiplicity is the Verma-flag multiplicity of
[[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]], and the right-hand
multiplicity is the simple composition multiplicity of the Verma module
$M(\mu)$ ([[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]]).

Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked based/global lattice suppliers.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], with source
parameter $s$, monomial basis $M_A$, ordinary bar $\psi$, source
dual-canonical family $L_A$, canonical family $T_A$, and the source forms
$\langle-,-\rangle$, $C$.

The highest vector $M_{A_\Lambda}$ generates the multiplicity-one constituent
$V(\Lambda)\subseteq F(\Lambda)$, and there is its normalized module projection
$\pi:F(\Lambda)\to V(\Lambda)$.

(1) The vectors $S_A:=\pi M_A$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, form a basis of
$V(\Lambda)$, and $D_A:=\pi L_A$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ form the
**source dual-canonical basis** of $V(\Lambda)$.

(2) What vanishes is $\pi L_A$ for $A$ not standard; $\pi M_A$ need not vanish
for nonstandard $A$. The integral kernel of $\pi$ is the saturated direct
summand with basis the $L_A$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, and
$\pi(F_{\mathcal A})$ has the actual basis $D_A$ (also $S_A$ on
$\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$), the source upper/costandard lattice. For every $B$,
$$\pi M_B=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(s)\,D_A,$$
which gives the explicit straightening of nonstandard projected monomials.

(3) All bases and maps commute with upper cuts and common-tail embeddings, so
the assertions hold in the full direct limit. The relation of the source
$D_A$ to the library form-dual upper family
([[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]]) is the explicit weight
rescaling proved in the global-basis comparison, not an unqualified
identification.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and $I$ bounded below. The
standard-class map $[M(A)]\mapsto M_A$ identifies the direct-sum $K_0$ of the
genuine tableau parabolic blocks with the full integral Fock module, with
matching multiset degrees and the residue Chevalley action of
$\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$. For every projective $P$ and finite-length $N$,
$$\dim\operatorname{Hom}(P,N)=\langle[P],[N]\rangle\quad\text{at }s=1 .$$
In particular $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$; no false standard/simple
orthogonality $\langle M_A,L_B\rangle=\delta$ is asserted. The projective,
simple and tilting basis identifications are proved separately.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the genuine tableau
$K_0$/Fock identification at $s=1$
([[thm-the-parabolic-o-grothendieck-group-is-the-integral-fock-module]]). For
every label $A$,
$$[L(A)]=L_A,\qquad [P(A)]=P_A,\qquad [T(A)]=T_A .$$
The projective coefficients are $d_{A,B}(1)$ by BGG reciprocity; the tilting
coefficients are the **opposite/reverse-column** composition coefficients
$\widetilde d_{A,B}(1)$, by the exact parabolic Ringel equivalence. They are not
generally the inverse-transpose of the original composition matrix. Simples,
projectives and tiltings therefore give the dual-canonical, quasi-canonical and
canonical Fock families respectively. These are ungraded specializations; no
Koszul grading and no identification of the library upper and lower families is
asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra and let $\mu$ be a highest weight. The action of
$U(\mathfrak g)$ on the Verma module $M(\mu)$ induces an algebra isomorphism
$$U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\mu\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \bigl(\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}M(\mu)\bigr)^{\operatorname{ad}\mathfrak g\text{-finite}},$$
where the target is the locally finite part of the endomorphism algebra for
the adjoint action $x\mapsto[x,-]$. In particular
$\operatorname{Ann}M(\mu)=U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\mu$. Moreover, for every
finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $E$,
$$\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),E\otimes M(\mu))=\dim E_0,$$
and the action identifies each finite adjoint isotypic multiplicity with that
dimension.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory
([[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

Fix a regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$ as in
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]], with
inclusion $\operatorname{incl}_\lambda:\mathcal O_\lambda\to\mathcal O$ and
exact projection $\operatorname{pr}_\lambda:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_\lambda$
of [[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], so that
$\operatorname{pr}_\lambda\circ\operatorname{incl}_\lambda=\operatorname{id}$;
the block is a direct summand of $\mathcal O$ and contains the projective
covers $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ of [[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]]. For a
finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module $E$ define
the endofunctor
$$F_E:=\operatorname{pr}_\lambda\circ(E\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_\lambda\colon\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow\mathcal O_\lambda .$$

**Basic properties.** The functor $F_E$ is well defined and additive:
$E\otimes-$ is an exact endofunctor of $\mathcal O$ and maps $\mathcal O$ into
itself ([[prop-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-category-o]]),
and $\operatorname{pr}_\lambda$ is exact. Hence $F_E$ is exact as a composite of
exact functors. It preserves projective objects: if $P\in\mathcal O_\lambda$ is
projective, then $E\otimes P$ is projective in $\mathcal O$
([[lem-tensoring-a-projective-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-is-projective]]),
and $\operatorname{pr}_\lambda$ preserves projectives
([[lem-block-projection-preserves-projectives]]). The identity module $E=0$
gives the zero functor, and $E=\mathbb C$ the identity functor, since the
one-dimensional trivial module acts by the identity.

**Projective functors.** A **projective functor** on
$\mathcal O_\lambda$ is an endofunctor of $\mathcal O_\lambda$ isomorphic to a
direct summand of some $F_E$, $E$ finite dimensional and
$\mathfrak h$-semisimple. Write $\mathcal F_\lambda$ for the full subcategory
of the endofunctor category of $\mathcal O_\lambda$ whose objects are the
projective functors, with arbitrary natural transformations as morphisms; it is
additive with the pointwise biproducts of [[def-additive-category]], and
"direct summand" means a pair of mutually inverse idempotent splittings as in
the idempotent-completion convention of that definition.

**Closure properties.** The class of projective functors is closed under
finite direct sums, composition, direct summands and passage to adjoints:

1. $F_{E\oplus E'}\cong F_E\oplus F_{E'}$, since tensoring with a direct sum
distributes over direct sums and $\operatorname{pr}_\lambda$ is additive.
2. $F_E\circ F_{E'}\cong F_{E\otimes E'}$: inserting
$\operatorname{incl}_\lambda\circ\operatorname{pr}_\lambda$ between the two
factors and using the associativity of the tensor product of finite-dimensional
modules identifies the composite with
$\operatorname{pr}_\lambda\circ((E\otimes E')\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_\lambda$.
3. $F_{E^*}$ is both a left and a right adjoint of $F_E$: this is
[[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]] applied to
the two generalized central characters of the block, since
$F_{E^*}=\operatorname{pr}_\lambda\circ(E^*\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_\lambda$
is the translation functor $T_{\chi_\lambda,E^*,\chi_\lambda}$ and similarly for
$F_E$.
4. A direct summand of an exact additive functor is exact, and a direct summand
of a functor preserving projective objects again preserves projective objects:
apply the splitting to the image of each object. Hence every projective functor
is exact and preserves projective objects, and the class is closed under
composition and finite direct sums.

This is the definition of Bernstein-Gelfand [BGe, Section 3.1] and of
[Soe90, Section 1.2]; unlike the functors $T_\lambda^\mu$ of
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], projective functors are not
required to come from a single finite-dimensional tensor functor, only from a
direct summand of one.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. In the deformed family of
[[def-the-deformed-category-o-family-and-its-specializations]] with $T$ a
localization of $S=S(\mathfrak h)$ and $M,N\in\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$:

1. The canonical map
$$U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_ZT\longrightarrow\bigl(\operatorname{End}_T(M_T(\lambda))\bigr)^{\mathfrak g\text{-finite}},\qquad u\otimes t\longmapsto\bigl(m\mapsto u\cdot m\cdot t\bigr),$$
is an isomorphism of $T$-algebras, the superscript denoting the $\mathfrak g$-finite part for the adjoint action $X\cdot f=X\circ f-f\circ X$, and the center $Z=Z(U(\mathfrak g))$ acting on $T$ through the shifted Harish-Chandra isomorphism $\operatorname{HC}_\rho$ ([[thm-harish-chandra-isomorphism-for-the-center]]) followed by evaluation at $\lambda+\rho+\epsilon$ on the universal parameter $\epsilon$.
2. For finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-modules $E,F$, the $T$-module
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(E\otimes M_T(\lambda),F\otimes M_T(\lambda))$
is free of rank $\dim(E\otimes F^{*})_0$, and the natural base-change map
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(M,N)\otimes_T\kappa(\epsilon)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes\kappa(\epsilon)}(M\otimes_T\kappa(\epsilon),N\otimes_T\kappa(\epsilon))$$
is an isomorphism for every $\epsilon\in\operatorname{Spec}T$.
3. $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(M,N)$ is locally free of finite rank over $T$.
4. If a $\mathfrak g\otimes R$-linear map of objects of $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ is an isomorphism on the special fiber at $0$, it is an isomorphism.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

For the abelian category [[thm-category-o-is-abelian-and-extension-closed]], define $K_0(\mathcal O)$ as the free abelian group on isomorphism classes $[M]$, modulo $[B]=[A]+[C]$ for every short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$. A set of representatives suffices: every finitely generated $U(\mathfrak g)$-module is a quotient of some $U(\mathfrak g)^n$, and those quotients form a set up to isomorphism.

Define the formal character by $\operatorname{ch}M=\sum_\mu(\dim M_\mu)e^\mu$. By [[prop-equivalent-support-description-of-category-o]], its integer coefficients are finite and supported in finitely many downward cones. Let $\mathscr R$ be the group of all such integer coefficient families, with pointwise addition. It is a ring with $e^\mu e^\nu=e^{\mu+\nu}$: at a fixed resulting weight, in any pair of cones the equation $\beta+\gamma=\eta$ with $\beta,\gamma\in Q^+$ has finitely many solutions, since every simple-root coefficient is bounded. Taking weight spaces is exact, so character gives a well-defined homomorphism $K_0(\mathcal O)\to\mathscr R$. The zero object's class and character are zero.

Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring. Then the polynomial ring $R[x]$ is a
Noetherian commutative ring.

No hypothesis beyond Noetherianity is placed on $R$: it may have zero divisors,
and it may be the zero ring.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. A left $R$-module $I$ is injective if and only if every homomorphism $f:J\to I$ from a left ideal $J\le R$ extends to a homomorphism $R\to I$.

The forward implication is choice-free. The converse uses AC through Zorn's lemma.

Every finite-dimensional representation of a finite-dimensional semisimple
Lie algebra over any characteristic-zero field is completely reducible.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
published root-space and $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ suppliers. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a
finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra
$\mathfrak h$, root system $\Phi$
([[thm-the-root-set-is-a-reduced-crystallographic-root-system]],
[[thm-root-space-decomposition-of-a-complex-semisimple-lie-algebra]],
[[thm-root-spaces-of-a-complex-semisimple-lie-algebra-are-one-dimensional]]),
positive system $\Phi^+$ with base of simple roots
$\Delta=\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r\}$
([[def-positive-system-and-base-of-simple-roots]],
[[def-reduced-crystallographic-euclidean-root-system]]), and let $J$ be a
subset of the simple indices $\{1,\dots,r\}$. Write $\Phi_J$ for the root
subsystem spanned by the simple roots indexed by $J$,
$$\Phi_J=\Phi\cap\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{\alpha_j:j\in J\},$$
and let $H_j=h_{\alpha_j}\in\mathfrak h$ be the coroot of $\alpha_j$
([[def-coroot-of-a-lie-algebra-root]] via
[[def-killing-dual-vector-of-a-root]]). Put
$$\mathfrak h_J=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{H_j:j\in J\},\qquad \mathfrak z_J=\{h\in\mathfrak h:\alpha_j(h)=0\text{ for all }j\in J\},$$
and define the following subspaces of $\mathfrak g$, where $\mathfrak g_\alpha$
is the root space of $\alpha$
([[thm-root-space-decomposition-of-a-complex-semisimple-lie-algebra]]):

$$\mathfrak s_J=\mathfrak h_J\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi_J}\mathfrak g_\alpha,\qquad \mathfrak l_J=\mathfrak s_J\oplus\mathfrak z_J=\mathfrak h\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi_J}\mathfrak g_\alpha,$$
$$\mathfrak u_J=\bigoplus_{\beta\in\Phi^+\smallsetminus\Phi_J^+}\mathfrak g_\beta,\qquad \mathfrak v_J=\bigoplus_{\beta\in\Phi^-\smallsetminus\Phi_J^-}\mathfrak g_\beta,\qquad \mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J .$$

Here $\Phi_J^\pm=\Phi_J\cap\Phi^\pm$ and $\Phi^\pm$ are the positive and
negative roots with $\mathfrak n^\pm$, $\mathfrak b$ as in
[[def-positive-and-negative-nilpotent-subalgebras-and-borel-subalgebra]]. The
construction depends only on the positive system and on $J$. The following
structural facts are part of the definition (proofs and references in the
Remarks; $\operatorname{rad}$ and $\operatorname{nilrad}$ are those of
[[def-radical-of-a-finite-dimensional-lie-algebra]] and
[[def-nilradical-of-a-finite-dimensional-lie-algebra]]).

**(1) Decomposition of the Cartan.** $\mathfrak h=\mathfrak h_J\oplus\mathfrak z_J$
and $\dim\mathfrak h_J=|J|$, so $\dim\mathfrak z_J=r-|J|$.

**(2) The semisimple part.** $\mathfrak s_J$ is a Lie subalgebra of
$\mathfrak g$; it is semisimple, and its root system with respect to the
Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h_J$ is $\Phi_J$, with positive system
$\Phi_J^+$ and Weyl group $W_J=\langle s_j:j\in J\rangle\le W$
([[def-weyl-group-of-a-root-system]],
[[def-cg-parabolic-quotient-and-two-sided-minima]]).

**(3) The reductive Levi algebra.** $\mathfrak l_J$ is a Lie subalgebra with
root system $\Phi_J$ relative to $\mathfrak h$; it is reductive as in
[[def-simple-semisimple-and-reductive-lie-algebras]], with center
$\mathfrak z_J$ and derived algebra $[\mathfrak l_J,\mathfrak l_J]=\mathfrak s_J$;
$\mathfrak h$ is a Cartan subalgebra of $\mathfrak l_J$ and the Weyl group of
$(\mathfrak l_J,\mathfrak h)$ is $W_J$. The algebra $\mathfrak l_J$ need not
be semisimple: its center $\mathfrak z_J$ is nonzero as soon as $J\ne\{1,\dots,r\}$.

**(4) Parabolic and radicals.** $\mathfrak l_J$, $\mathfrak u_J$, $\mathfrak v_J$
and $\mathfrak p_J$ are Lie subalgebras
([[prop-brackets-of-root-spaces]]); $\mathfrak u_J$ is an ideal of
$\mathfrak p_J$, $\mathfrak l_J$ stabilizes $\mathfrak u_J$ and $\mathfrak v_J$,
and $\mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak l_J\ltimes\mathfrak u_J$ is a semidirect product
([[def-levi-subalgebra-and-levi-decomposition]]). Moreover
$\operatorname{nilrad}(\mathfrak p_J)=\mathfrak u_J$ and
$$\operatorname{rad}(\mathfrak p_J)=\mathfrak z_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J .$$
Consequently $[\mathfrak p_J,\mathfrak p_J]=\mathfrak s_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$
and the quotient $\mathfrak p_J/\operatorname{rad}(\mathfrak p_J)\cong\mathfrak s_J$
is semisimple: in the sense of
[[def-levi-subalgebra-and-levi-decomposition]], $\mathfrak s_J$ is a semisimple
Levi factor of $\mathfrak p_J$ and $\mathfrak l_J$ is the reductive complement
to the nilradical. The parabolic $\mathfrak p_J$ contains $\mathfrak b$ and
$\mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak b\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi_J^-}\mathfrak g_\alpha$,
the span of the negative root spaces of $\Phi_J$; for $J=\varnothing$ one has
$\mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak b$, and for $J=\{1,\dots,r\}$ one has
$\mathfrak l_J=\mathfrak s_J=\mathfrak g$ and
$\mathfrak u_J=\mathfrak v_J=0$.

**(5) The positive grading.** There exists $\zeta\in\mathfrak z_J$ with
$\alpha_j(\zeta)=0$ for $j\in J$ and $\alpha_i(\zeta)=1$ for $i\notin J$. With
respect to $\operatorname{ad}(\zeta)$ every root space $\mathfrak g_\beta$ has
weight $\beta(\zeta)$, so:

* $\mathfrak l_J$ has degree $0$ (all of $\Phi_J$ vanishes on $\zeta$);
* $\mathfrak u_J$ has strictly positive integral degrees
  $\beta(\zeta)\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$;
* $\mathfrak v_J$ has strictly negative integral degrees.

In particular $\mathfrak u_J$ is nilpotent by this positive grading, and both
$\mathfrak u_J$ and $\mathfrak v_J$ have finite-dimensional fixed-degree
slices of their PBW algebras:
$\dim U(\mathfrak u_J)_d<\infty$ and $\dim U(\mathfrak v_J)_d<\infty$ for
every $d\in\mathbb Z$ ([[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]]).

derivations.claim: Let U=U(m), I=I_chi. Replace x by y=x−chi(x). These shifted generators have the original brackets, because chi vanishes on brackets. Choose a basis adapted to the lower-central filtration, with weight w_i the largest lower-central index containing its basis vector. PBW reordering and the commutator formula show that I^n is spanned by ordered monomials of total lower-central weight≥n: one inclusion follows from reordering n factors, while the reverse follows because each basis vector of weight w lies in I^w, being a linear combination of iterated brackets of length w.

The Rees algebra R=⊕_(n≥0) I^n t^n is generated by y_i t^r, 0≤r≤w_i. Their span is a finite-dimensional Lie algebra: a nonzero bracket component y_k has w_k≥w_i+w_j, so r+s≤w_k. PBW gives its enveloping algebra a polynomial associated graded. For any left ideal, Hilbert basis gives finitely many generators of its homogeneous leading ideal; lift them and subtract matching highest-degree terms until the nonnegative degree decreases to zero. The lifts generate the original ideal. Thus the enveloping algebra is left noetherian, and its surjection onto R makes R left noetherian. For a left ideal J⊂U, ⊕(J∩I^n)t^n is a graded left ideal of R and has finitely many homogeneous generators. For fixed k, choosing n greater than k plus their largest degrees gives J∩I^n⊂I^k J. This is the precise Artin–Rees consequence needed here.

Set E_chi=∪_(n≥0)(U/I^n)^*, with left action (x f)(r)=f(r x). To prove injectivity, take a U-linear map phi:J→E_chi. U is noetherian, so choose finitely many generators of J. A common I^k kills their images and hence all images, since I is two-sided. The scalar functional lambda(j)=phi(j)(1) kills I^k J. Choose n with J∩I^n⊂I^k J, extend lambda from J/(J∩I^n) to U/I^n, and call the extension a∈E_chi. The map U→E_chi, u↦u a, extends phi, because at r its value on j is a(rj)=phi(rj)(1)=phi(j)(r). Baer's criterion gives injectivity. This supplies the injective-continuous-dual assertion cited without proof in BK Lemma8.20.

For a U(m)-finitely generated g-module X, evaluation at1 identifies Hom_m(X,E_chi) with the scalar functionals lambda:X→C that kill I^n X for some n. Indeed, reconstruct the map by F_lambda(v)(r)=lambda(rv); finitely many generators give a common n. The right U(g)-action is (lambda·u)(v)=lambda(uv). On E-valued maps its formula is therefore
(F·u)(v)(r)=lambda(u r v),
not the generally non-m-linear expression F(uv)(r)=lambda(r u v). This distinguishes the compressed scalar-functional notation in the source from a literal E-valued composition.

The right action preserves continuity. For a fixed u∈U(g), the finite PBW subspace generated by all iterated ad m on u is finite-dimensional and its negative-column action is nilpotent; sufficiently long products of ad m vanish. Moving u past a product of sufficiently many shifted m generators therefore leaves at least n of them on the left. Equivalently u I^(n+C)⊂I^n U(g) for some C=C(u). Thus lambda u kills I^(n+C)X. On this continuous-dual module the right shifted m-action is locally nilpotent. Injectivity of E_chi makes Hom_m(−,E_chi) exact, and right Skryabin makes its Whittaker vectors exact. These Whittaker vectors are precisely Hom_m(X,C_chi). Dualizing this finite-dimensional vector space gives an exact covariant functor.

The restricted dual uses the row-sum torus a=span{Σ_(row(j)=r)E_jj}, not the full Cartan and not the column-origin vector c. Every e-adjacent pair lies in one row, so chi has a-weight0. If X is generated over U(m) by finitely many a-weight spaces, an m-linear functional into C_chi vanishes outside those finitely many weights: lambda(uv)=chi(u)lambda(v), and chi(u)=0 in every nonzero a-weight. Thus the restricted-dual definition agrees with the entire finite-dimensional Hom space. Generalized parabolic Vermas are U(m)-free on a finite-dimensional Levi module by PBW; their finite projective flags/presentations from the repaired parabolic highest-weight supplier make every genuine parabolic O object finitely generated over U(m). This establishes exactness on precisely that category.

For X=U(g)⊗_(U(p))X_0, the Hom space is canonically X_0^*. The finite-W action on its covariant dual uses the right-model head twist eta_head(E_jj)=E_jj+n−Σ_(k≤col(j))q_k. The left-model twist is eta_tail(E_jj)=E_jj+n−Σ_(k≥col(j))q_k. Their numerical difference is −tr_m(ad E_jj), since the trace counts earlier minus later column heights. This numerical identity does not by itself prove equality of the two W models. The actual identification of the left/right W models and compatibility on all shifted-Yangian generators is the explicit matrix-generator check in the companion finite-W matrix note; the vector-space duality alone does not supply it.

Reflect the pyramid and transpose matrix units with its column-renumbering permutation. This is an anti-isomorphism of U(g). Reversing each path preserves its degree, sign and cut inequalities and sends P_ij;x to P'_ji;x term by term. The shift matrix is transposed. The preceding reflected generator theorem therefore identifies the reflected W and the transpose images of the original generators. Applying this anti-isomorphism to its left reduction condition turns the left ideal into the right ideal and its tail shift into the original head shift. Consequently the SAME original W subalgebra equals {u:[eta_head(u),m]⊂I_chi U(g)}. Numerically eta_head−eta_tail=−tr_m ad on each diagonal matrix; this equality is explained by the column counts but is not used as a substitute for the path-transpose proof.

Fix an admissible origin: c_j−c_k integral implies c_j=c_k. The original arbitrary-origin deformed tensor algebra remains separate and unrestricted. In a column of height q whose global row numbers are n−q+1,…,n, write its strict entries a_1,…,a_q. The genuine head-model V action makes its finite-Levi highest weight nu_s=a_s+n−q+s−1. This follows directly from the global highest weight lambda_i=a_i+i−1 and eta_head diagonal shift n−q_1−…−q_col: the column-reading position i=q_before+(global_row−n+q) gives lambda_i+eta_head=a_i+global_row−1.
Finite-Levi Weyl gives, on row variables z_(n−q+1),…,z_n,
ch L(nu)=det(z_r^(nu_s+q−s))/det(z_r^(q−s)) =(Π_(r=n−q+1)^n z_r^(n−1)) det(z_r^(a_s))/det(z_r^(q−s)).

The numerator exponent is exactly a_s+n−1; the column height and reading offset cancel. The prefactor and denominator are independent of the entries. Products over columns therefore identify the row-torus character of V(N(A)) with a fixed factor times products of nested bottom-row flag minors, evaluated at y_(r,a)=z_r^a. For the ground column a_s=c+1−(n−q+s), the determinant cancels the Vandermonde and gives precisely Π z_r^c, verifying the origin normalization.

All exponential expressions lie in the group algebra of the finite subgroup generated by their occurring complex weights and the integral row weights. That subgroup is finitely generated and torsion free, hence free abelian; its group algebra is a Laurent polynomial domain. The nonzero Vandermonde may therefore be cancelled. A zero character of an actual nonzero finite-dimensional module is impossible: its coefficients are nonnegative weight dimensions, and evaluation of the group algebra at1 is its positive dimension.

Fix a finite entry alphabet U, and introduce independent variables y_(r,a), with row space C^n and entry space U. Antisymmetrizing each column of a tensor gives its bottom-row minor, and multiplying gives a GL(U)-linear map from the column-wedge tensor F to Sym(C^n⊗U). Each minor is killed by the lower-row raising operators: replacing a present row by a later row duplicates a row inside its bottom-row set. The product has row weight (p_1,…,p_n).

Classical Cauchy decomposition follows from the actual published Schur–Weyl decomposition: identify the degree-N symmetric power with diagonal S_N invariants of (C^n)^tensor N⊗U^tensor N, then use the two Specht decompositions. The needed self-duality is complex linear: polytabloids have real coefficients, so their span is conjugation-stable; the bilinear tabloid form B(v,w)=sum v_T w_T is invariant and B(v,conjugate(v)) is the positive Hermitian norm. It is therefore nondegenerate on the Specht span. Schur's lemma with this explicit bilinear duality leaves one multiplicity space for each matching partition. The lower-row highest-weight line at (p_1,…,p_n) selects the partition (p_n,…,p_1), so the entire flag-minor image lies in the irreducible entry module of highest weight Lambda=Σ_j omega_(q_j). The ground product of minors is a nonzero polynomial. Hence the image is exactly this irreducible module. Actual16 proves that this constituent occurs once in F; therefore this nonzero normalized map has exactly the kernel of actual16's highest-component projection pi. No quantum flag algebra or quantum Peter–Weyl theorem is imported.

For different complex cosets, first apply the companion typed category equivalence and use one independent set of variables for each coset. The same Cauchy proof applies to each coset's columns, with their retained sorted heights. Multiplication across the disjoint variable sets is injective on the tensor product. Thus the kernel is the sum of the component projection kernels, exactly the off-standard lower-basis kernel of the product of actual16 models. The shift a↦a−c_kappa+n−n_kappa and inf I_kappa=1−n_kappa is explicit in that companion proof.

V is exact on the genuine parabolic category and sends N(A) to its finite-Levi standard V(A). Actual16 identifies [L_O(A)] with its source lower/dual-canonical vector L_A at parameter1. Its projection pi L_A is zero exactly off Std. The preceding flag-minor factorization consequently gives zero row-torus character of V(L_O(A)) for every off-standard A. Positivity of actual module characters makes V(L_O(A))=0.

The kernel of the Grothendieck map of V is stable under every residue e/f operator, because the actual tensor identity and Casimir/flip compatibility give V e=e V and V f=f Wh. Thus after quotienting by the already-known off-standard kernel, any additional kernel would be a submodule of actual16's irreducible highest component (or the irreducible tensor product for the direct sum of coset root algebras). The ground class survives: its V image is the one-dimensional C_c by the induced-module computation. Hence no additional kernel exists. Every Std simple therefore has a nonzero V image. This argument does not presume that image simple, does not rely on injectivity of the exponential evaluation on the entire abstract polynomial module, and does not require a classification of all finite-dimensional W simples.

Take finite alphabets containing the relevant finite labels and tensor words, with the proved boundary block projections; actual16 gives compatibility under enlarging the cuts. The argument applies on each cut and hence to every object in the selected finite degree/category. All comparisons use integer order within a coset, not an order on C.

The ground P_c is a simple projective-injective by the actual16 integral model and the typed coset product. Tensor biadjunction makes T=P_c⊗V^tensor d projective-injective. Its indecomposable summands are precisely the Std prinjectives, with possible multiplicities; it is a detecting object, not a generator of the whole parabolic category.

Hd acts on T by the universal tensor Casimir. At the first tensor step, the finite p flag of V has one standard section for each column. On its jth section, the Casimir identity Omega=(C_total−C_source−C_V)/2 gives eigenvalue c_j+q_j−n. The column-order flag therefore makes Π_j(x_1−(c_j+q_j−n)) annihilate T; the remaining factors are untouched at higher degree. Thus the cyclotomic action genuinely exists on T, not merely on its V image M=V_c^tensor d. The explicit V tensor comparison transports this action to M.

The filtered Vust theorem gives End_W(M)^op=B, the cyclotomic tensor image. V maps End_g(T)^op into B, and its image contains B because every Hecke operator came from T. This map is injective: a nonzero endomorphism has nonzero image inside T; that image has a Std socle factor by actual16 prinjectivity, so exact V with its established simple kernel cannot kill it. Thus End_g(T)^op=B.

Choose a full finite projective generator Q of the genuine O summand containing T as an explicit summand and write its algebra as A; the projector onto T is e and B=eAe. The exact Schur functor is e(−). It kills precisely the offStd simples. Its left adjoint Ae⊗_B− is right exact and satisfies e(Ae⊗X)=X. The counit Ae⊗eN→N has kernel and cokernel killed by e. Applying V sends it to an isomorphism. Therefore V factors through e(−), and its factor F on B-mod is naturally M⊗_B− by finite free presentations. This factor is exact: the only failure of exactness after the left adjoint is killed by e and hence by Wh. It is faithful, since every B-simple is eL_O(A) for a Std label and its V image is nonzero; exactness then detects every nonzero image of a morphism.

A finite-dimensional right B-module whose tensor functor is exact is projective. Explicitly, take its finite projective cover P→M with kernel K⊂P rad B. Tensor the inclusion K→P with B/rad B; flatness makes K/K rad B inject into P/P rad B, but this map is zero, so Nakayama gives K=0. Faithfulness forces every right indecomposable projective to occur in M: otherwise tensor with the corresponding left simple would vanish. Thus M_B is a progenerator. The first filtered centralizer identity gives Wd=End_B(M). The usual generator presentation/evaluation argument now gives the genuine Morita equivalence Wd-mod≃B-mod. In particular F sends B-simples to Wd-simples, proving the full relevant V simple-image claim without assuming it earlier.

Tensor compatibility follows from the continuous-dual evaluation, ordinary finite tensor adjunction and the actual balanced Skryabin map: its coproduct identity carries the Casimir and flips to the deformed tensor model. Thus $V(P_c)=\mathbb C_c$ and $V(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d})=V_c^{\otimes d}$. The normalized comparison is determined on the ground and its tensor words, hence on the detecting tensor bimodule and on finite free quotient presentations through the established exact Morita factorization. Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix the pyramid $\lambda$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, an origin $c\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$, and let
$V_c^{\otimes d}$ be the truncated tensor space of
[[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]. Let
$W_d=\varphi_d(W(\lambda))\subseteq\operatorname{End}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ be the
image of the finite W-algebra and let
$B_d=\psi_d(H_d(\Lambda))$ be the image of the cyclotomic Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] under the right action. Then:

1. $W_d$ and $B_d$ are mutual centralizers on $V_c^{\otimes d}$, for every
   complex origin $c$ and every $d$, and their associated graded image
   algebras are the corresponding images of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ and of the
   truncated polynomial/permutation algebra.
2. If $q_l\ge d$, then the action of the full cyclotomic algebra
   $H_d(\mathbf a)$ is faithful.
3. If $c$ is admissible (that is, $c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$),
   then the tensor module is a progenerator and
   $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is a Morita equivalence
   between $W_d$-mod and $B_d$-mod.

Mutual centralizers alone do not imply Morita for arbitrary $c$: the explicit
example with $c=(0,1)$, $q=(1,1)$, $d=2$ on the companion page has a
nonprojective tensor module.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector
space, let $e\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ be nilpotent with largest
Jordan string length $l\ge1$, let $d\ge0$, and put $E=V^{\otimes d}$. Let
$$B=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$$
act on $E$ by the individual operators $x_i=e$ (in the $i$-th tensor factor)
and the place permutations, and let
$\varphi\colon U(\mathfrak g^e)\to\operatorname{End}(E)$ be the algebra map
induced by the diagonal action of $\mathfrak g^e=\{X:[X,e]=0\}$ and
$\psi\colon B\to\operatorname{End}(E)^{\mathrm{op}}$ the map encoding the
right action. Then
$$\varphi(U(\mathfrak g^e))=\operatorname{End}_B(E),\qquad \operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g^e}(E)^{\mathrm{op}}=\psi(B),$$
for every nilpotent Jordan type and every $d$. If $e$ has at least $d$ Jordan
strings of the maximum length $l$, then $\psi$ is injective. For $d=0$ the
identities are scalar identities and injectivity is automatic.

The full converse uses the proved normality and covariant-extension suppliers
of this page; it is not a stable-only claim and it does not assume the double
commutant identity.

**degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is the quotient
$$H_d(\mathbf a):=H_d\Big/\Bigl(\prod_{j=1}^l(x_1-a_j)\Bigr),$$
the two-sided ideal being the one generated by the displayed polynomial
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]],
[[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the tensor-realization verification below; the quotient definition itself is choice-free.

The verification below records the structure of $H_d(\mathbf a)$ used on this
page. A $\mathbb C$-basis is given by the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad 0\le r_1,\dots,r_d<l,\ w\in S_d,$$
so that $\dim H_d(\mathbf a)=l^dd!$; the polynomial-degree filtration has
associated graded the algebra
$\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$. For
integral roots $a_j\in\mathbb Z$ this is the cyclotomic quotient $H_d(\Lambda)$
attached to the dominant weight $\Lambda=\sum_j m_j\Lambda_j$ of the integer
type-A root system, with $m_j=\#\{i:a_i=j\}$; for general complex roots one
uses a separate integer chain in each coset of $\mathbb C/\mathbb Z$, and the
symbol $\Lambda_a$ denotes a formal fundamental weight on that chain, not an
index of the integer-only lattice. The pyramid roots of the finite-W-algebra
constructions are $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ for the origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ and the
pyramid columns $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$. If $l=1$, then
$x_j=a_1+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j)$ in the quotient. The generator-fixing
anti-involution of $H_d$ descends to $H_d(\mathbf a)$. The top coefficient
functional of the monomial basis is a nondegenerate symmetric trace on
$H_d(\mathbf a)$, and it restricts to a nondegenerate trace on every central
block corner.
